Worked heel obedience on and off leash. Getting much better in both.

bizi did well on the down in motion and three phase out, he also did well when recalled off the bite.
Outdoor area search, hidden under board.
Indoor packages on the floor. Rocky went straight to source without issues.

Was hidden inside the glove box of the vehicle. Rocky indicated on the back driver side door first, then when placed inside of the vehicle, went straight to glove box, first smelling up near windshield then under it.
Was hidden under the stove in the drawer. Rocky sat on fridge across from it. Re-searched the area, he then laid and on stove drawer.
Was hidden inside of heater in bathroom. Rocky went straight to source and scratched and sat.
Was hidden under the hood of the vehicle. Rocky indicated under the front wheel fender. Was allowed to call this because he was directly under the source but we could not get to it.

Rocky went back to aggressive alert on backpack where hide was at. Pulle him off it for a few minutes then started search over again to make sure he wasn't just biting backpack. He went back to the backpack and started biting it once again. I called this as the hide.
Hide was under the trailer on the frame. Rocky crawled up under the trailer and did not sit but could tell he was in odor. He eventually pulled the entire hide down to the ground.
This was a building search with a bark alert. Rocky was sent in the building and began to bark at the door where the agitator was at. Agitator was in the bathroom
Open area search of a field with the agitator hidding in the tall grass behind the fence where the dog could not get to him. Once again Rocky had to bark to indicate he had located the agitator.

Did 5 minute down and stay no issues with that. Also did on and off leash heel with right, left and about turn X2. Did very well with on leash. During off leash when I was in a jog, he wanted to run out in front of me a little bit but did stay with me. Will need to work this more often with him.
Straight bite with a call off, no issues with this.
Down in motion and Call off without contact. He went all the way through on the first one, had to do some corrective work with him, but was able to get it fixed and passed him on second attempt.

Handler Protection drill - Rocky did not have any issues with this until the call off. Did not want to let go of bite. Had to work some corrections with him on this and was able to pass him off the second attempt with it.
Had to fire 2 rounds with the gun with Rocky off-leash. He could not run away or attack the gun. He jumped but did not run off.
Rocky had to jump over abench and then go into a down on the other side and wait for me while I came around and picked him up. He did as was needed of him.
Door popper drills in the dark. Had him run to my location in several different areas on the grass near the baseball field and then down near me. Only rewarded him with the ball on the very last one.

Did more on and off leash obedience. Still going to need much more work with the off leash while moving at a faster pace, wants to run out in front of me still instead of staying at a heel. May try using hotdogs next time.
Dry send into the building, did not actually send him in, only went to the door, had him down, gave commands at entrance to make sure he remained quiet then prasied him up and left.
exterior vehicle search found underhood.
bathroom search found in heater systemtic search was not used k9 alerted and sat

K9 showed that he could jump over object hurdling a bench.
gunfire drill with k9 off leash, k9 stay in a down by my side and didn’t lundge for the weapon or try to run away

k9 was sent on a bite and commanded to release after he had bit using a three phase out - Stand still, Don’t move and laydown. K9 completed task great
suspect attacked me the handler and the k9 jumped inbetween to bite the suspect. The drill was done great k9 did as he was suppose to.
took K9 on a half mile track in the mountians. K9 came off track but quickly got back on and stayed on until the end.

Off leash obedience outside and inside of the residence. He did very well for the most part as far as listening to what was being told what to do. Could tell he was starting to get a little more anxious so put him up in his kennel to let him calm down.

Worked tatical obedience around the house while doing silent recalls with e-collar. Did very well.
Bark drills with 3 phase out. No issues.

With the weather starting to change and get colder. I am going back to using hot dogs as a training aid for tracking. I want Rocky to learn to track in the colder weather as well. Starting off with shorter tracks with a shorter cook time on them. Will progressivly get longer tracks with longer wait times. This was from hot dog to hot dog across the cold almost frozen grass.

Worked on his down and stay, heeling on leash, and some tatical obedience at the house. Would place him in a down and have him remain there for 10 min intervals. He would break at times from distractions in the area such as the cats, would correct him and bring him back to the area and place him back in a down. He was getting better at it all.

Down in motion using the balls. He did not do as well as I wanted this time. He kept running through the command to get the ball. Would correct him and he kept going. Finally got him to do a good down in motion, rewarded him on it by throwing in the second ball and letting him play with it. Ended on this good note with him.

Entire thing of scent logic was placed inside of a cupboard in a tupperware container with cotton and cardboard around it. Hamburger was also being cooked in the same area at the time of the search. Rocky ignored everything else when given the command to search. I allowed him to search off leash. As he was passing by the cupboard, he had a head jerk and went to bracketing on it until he got to the area the hide was in. He then did a stand and stare. I tried getting him to sit and instead he laid down in a stare at the source. He was given his reward.  I will work more sit drills with him.

3 cotton balls with the odor on them were placed inside the air vent on the floor. Rocky was given the command to search and I could tell he was in odor but he could not figure out where it was coming from. I began to detail around the area not going straight to the vent but allowing him to work around the area for it. When I got to the area of the ven, I presented a small picture frame area above the vent. He went up to sniff it but then came back down and with the way he was sniffing the area at this point I could tell he was in odor. He was sniffing the wall trying to find it. I allowed him time to try and find the source but he would not lower his nose far enough. I presented the vent and once I did he had no issues going to an alert on it. Again he laid down and stared. Reward was given.

Placed several hides of cottons balls with the odor of marijuana outside on several different vehicles in the parking lot near the front of the court house. Also had several vehicles that were searched as blanks in the parking lot as well. This was a sit drill with Rocky to work on him returning to a sit for his alert instead of doing a stand and stare or down and stare. I want him to go back to sit and stare. I ran him first on a blank vehicle to make sure he would not alert on it. He did not do so. The next one he was able to get into the odor quickly from the wind and first wanted to stand and stare at the source. These hides were easy to find for him to work the sit. I told him to sit and did not reward him until he did so. Once he did I rewared him. After playing with him for a minute. I then went to the next vehicle. It also had a hide in it. He hit the source of the odor and really slowly sat without me telling him to do so. I waited until his butt touched the ground before rewarding him. Once it touched reward was thrown in right away. The next several vehicles we searched after playing with him for a few minutes were all blank vehicles to again, make sure he would not alert to them. He did not alert on any of the vehicles. Last vehicle in the row had a hide in it. Once he was in odor he began to bracket the odor until he got to the source of it. Once there, without telling him or any kind of correction, he sat on his own very quickly. The second he did, he was given his reward. I allowed him to run around and play with it for some time because he did so well on that one. Ended on that note.

Laid another track using hot dogs again today. Still working on getting him used to tracking in the colder temps with the vegitation starting to die off for winter. It was also raining some on us and the temp was much cooler then it has been before (36 F) I also extended the track a little bit longer, going out about 50 yards this time and allowed it to sit 20 minutes before starting him on it. He was very hyper today while running the track, he came off it several times and I had to bring him back to it. Not sure if this is due to the weather or him being more hyper than normal. But after about the third time bringing him back to the track, he stayed on it with his nose to the ground and finished it out.

Hide was wrapped in plastic and paper and placed inside an old jail oven inside the boat shed. I allowed the hide to sit in there for an 45 minutes before allowing Rocky to search. Once he started to search he went passed the oven several times getting a head jerk on it but never alerting to it. I presented the area several times to him but he still did not alert. I believe I did not allow enough time to sit in the oven to allow the odor to come out enough of something built to be more air tight. I "burped" the door a little bit and once I did that, he had no issues alerting to it and alerted with a stand and stare. I gave him his reward at this point. I will need to work more sit drills with him. Get him back to alerting more with a sit and not a stand.

This was blank building search of the fire station to see how he would react and respond to it. There was a CPR dummy set up in the training room sitting on the floor with fire gear on that did in fact look like a person sitting there. I gave commands at the door and sent Rocky in. He did not go after the dummy in the room. I allowed him to search for some time and then I couldn't hear him running around anymore. I entered the through the building, clearing rooms as I went. Rocky had made it all the way back to the garage area of the fire station and was alerting to a drug hide I had out under a truck. He was in a sit on this and had been for sometime. I rewarded him for the find on his own.

3 hides were placed throughout the garage area of the fire station. All were cotton balls that had the odor on them. One was inside a boot of one of the fire fighters. Another was inside the light truck and the third was up under a fire truck near the drive line. Rocky was able to locate each of these. Hide was wrapped in plastic and hidden inside the storage unit itself. Storage unit #57. This was an indoor storage unit room with a total of 14 units inside. I called the lock area of the unit and was told that was not it but he was in the area. I allowed him to keep working it and he went to the lower corner of the unit placing his nose there and then alerting with a down and stare. I called that and this was correct. He was given his reward at this point. To make sure he did not give any improper responses, I continued to search the remaining 13 units that were blank. He never alerted to any of the others.

Hide was wrapped in plastic and placed in an outside storage unit. Unit #24. Started out by running Rocky down the row of units allowing him to free search them as we ran by them. He alerted to it with a sit and stare, staring at the bottom of the unit. I called this area which was correct. Rocky was given his reward. I then searched the remaning 17 units on the outside row to make sure he did not give any improper alerts. He did not do so.

Placed 2 hides in the bay area of the fire station. One was inside the side compartment of a fire truck. At that point he came running back to me and acted like he wanted to play running around in the living room area and then doing what he normally does when at home. I praised him up and we left.

While in the house. I  allowed Rocky to randomly wander around some but would place him in a down and stay at different times. I would then walk away into another room to see what he would do. He did very well with staying where I told him to stay. We did this for an hour straight. He only broke his down one time and that was when I placed him in a down in the middle of the living room and then I sat on the couch in front of him. He stayed in the down for 15 minutes before barking once and then getting up and coming over trying to climb on my lap. I corrected him back to where I had him placed him back in a down and had him stay there for another 5 minutes before I praised him up and allowed him to run around on his own again.

Placed a hide of cotton balls inside an Altoids container up under one of the picnic benches in the pavilion. I started the search out by placing Rocky down-wind of the hide. During this time, I felt the wind shift myself and Rocky then stopped searching the area the source was at and ran towards the corner of the pavilion. I could see leaves circling on the ground in the corner which tells me the air-flow was doing just that inside the pavilion. Rocky was very focused on the corner trying to locate the hide. He did not alert but was in odor. I then did a detailed search starting on one bench working down it towards the bench with the hide. Once we got to the hide, he placed his nose dirctly above where the hide was at and went straight to a sit. I rewarded him at this point.
Spent a little bit of time working his down and stay and working on his recall to me from different areas around the house. He did very well with these.

Laid a track for him and let it age for 45 minutes before starting him on it. He did his normal zig-zag while working the track but seemed to be doing well with it up until the end. Tatical obedience around the house. Also worked down and stay, on-leash, and off-leash obedience as well. Did well with everything.

Hide was 3 cotton balls inside an Altoids can that was placed up under the mailbox outside of the front of the courthouse. Wind was blowing from the south to the north. After placing his nose up under the bottom of the mailbox. He sat and stared at the source until reward was given.

Spent some time at the high school while working out west working on his down in motion. He did well with it so I did not spend a lot of time doing this. Allowed him at the end to run through and get the ball without giving him the command to go down.

Placed a hide inside an altoids can and then placed that inside a paper evidence bag. Hide was then hidden upstairs in the fire station in the back corner of the room. Once we got to the are where the hide was at I noticed the change in behavior with the head jerk and bracketing to try and get to source. After a few minutes he was able to get closer to it and and alerted on the hide. Reward was given.

Hide was wrapped in plastic bag and placed inside an old center console that was sitting on the floor of the sally port. Hide was placed inside an Altoids container and then placed up under the scissor lift in the sally port. When given the command to search the area, I allowed him to search without detailing anything. I allowed him to work it on his own without detailing anything as I wanted him to figure it out. He was able to work it as close as he possibly could get and then went to a sit. Reward was given.

Cotton balls with the odor were placed inside the vending machine where the soda comes out. When I started. I placed Rocky in a down and began to pre-search walk. As I was walking back to him, I could tell he was already in odor from 15 feet away. I gave him the command to search and he went staight to the source. He was able to open the bottom a little bit and then went to a sit and stare when I rewarded him.

Small velt pad was placed up under the motion sensor in the hallway going to Magistrate Court. Rocky located the source fairly quick (wasn't main options in the hallway) and ended up knocking it off the wall trying to get his toy to come out of it. I placed it on the ground and had him go to a sit alert before giving him his reward.

Cotton balls with odor were placed inside an altoids can that were then placed inside a garbage in the hallway near the courts. Rocky was given the command to search the area and during his free search first, as he ran pass the garbage can I noticed a change in behavior from him, a head snap back to the garbage can and then he kept sniffing the can several times. Bark drills. No issues. As soon as he seen the bite pillow he knew exactly what he needed to do in order to get it.
Worked on his obedience in the house. Worked his down and stay, his heeling and his sit. He did well with this. Each down and stay I went longer times.
Dry send into both containers I have on the property as a building search. Very easy for him to search these but used them as something different and to break things up some.

Dry send into the building as a building search. He did very well hunting throughout the entire building checking doors and areas as he went. Rewarded him by praising him up when we left.

Once he came back to me at the very end without a correction, I put him back in the vehicle and ended it there.

Was told this was correct. I had him go to a sit before giving him his reward.

Still had the cotton balls in the suitcase from the previous search. Took the cotton balls and placed them in the garage inside the cabinet sitting on the floor. Rocky was in odor but was having a hard time locating where it was coming from. I had to detail the area with more "detail" getting him to get his nose closer to the source. Once he got close to it, He began to work it on his own bracketing back and forth and would not leave that area. (crack in door) He finally went to a sit and I gave him his reward.
Worked his down and stay. He did very well with it and stayed for the first 10 minutes without issues. Ended it on that.

made bizi stay onmy right side while I worked on a few home projects. If he got bored and tried to leave my side I would give him the command to heel and make him stay next to me. Bizi did very well and stay by my side until released.

placed bizi in a down and then made him return to a sitting position to be rewarded. He is so use to go to a down to be rewarded or to be given a command that he would immediately go to a down. I worked with him on this for a little bit and it will still need work.

had bizi on a make shift leash tied to my waist tightly. When I moved he would move with out command. I made him stay on my right side and would be made to move with the tension on the leash whenevr I moved. Purpose of this excersise is to get bizi heeling with out command. Will keep working on this excersise.

hid a toy in the back yard while bizi was inside. I the wind was blowing hard and it was very cold. I hid the toy under a wood pile. I took bizi to where I started my track there was snow on the ground but not a lot. I gave bizi the command to search and he took off in the right direction but quickly moved off and couldn’t find the track he searched deligently before I prasied him for his efforts and took him inside. Due to the cold and snow I don’t think the ground produced enough odor for him to track. I will continue with this excersice

I placed Bizi in a down and moved to the end of my hallway. In the middle I placed a large bowl of food. I went to the end and stood at the end of the hallway waiting to release bizi from his down. When I was about to release bizi I showed him the toy and gave him the command to get the toy. Bizi bypassed the food and went for the toy I was holding. I played with him and then let him have the food.

attached bizi to my waist again for heeling without command. He did very well I give the heel command once and then move around the house and he stays right with me. I will do this a few more times before taking the leash away.

attached leash to my waist again and moved around the home. Half way through I unhoked the leash at first bizi stayed right on my side. He quickly relized that he was not attached and moved slightly away from me. He stayed on a heel but not as tight as he was with the leash

had a deputy put a tin can with a source in an open field. The was approximatley 2 inches of snow on the ground and it was 22 degrees the wind was blowing slightly. I started bizi in a grid search and moved back and fourth over the area. During this period Bizi kept trying to pull me to a trailer so I allowed him to go to the trailer. I remembered where I was and when he didn’t alert on anything I took him back to the area we left off on. We eventully came to the area where the tin can was and he went over it but quickly flipped around and located the source. He laid down indicating he had found the source and then hit the can with is nose.

had a deputy hide a source in a large shop building. The source was hidden under a lawn mower. The garage doors were open allowing air to pass through the building. The building was very large and there was a lot of items to search. I laid bizi down and did a walk through looking for obstacles. I gave biz the command to search while off leash. Bizi moved throught he building searching intensly and then got close to the lawn mower and his head flipped towards the mower and his mouth closed tighly and he moved around the mower slowly before stoping on the back left wheel and sat and stared. I informed the deputy that id call that as the hide and they indicated that he was correct.

had a deputy hide a source outside next to the building. I walked Bizi past the area without giving commands to see if he would pick up on the source. We walked far passed the area and bizi didn’t show any intrest. I got to the end of the building and turnaround and came back. On the way back bizi pulled me into the building and arund a bush. The source was set inside the bush. Bizi tried to get further into the bush where the source was until finally sitting and barking indicating that he was on source.

had a deputy place a source on a vehicle. I was given an area to search with 3 possible vehicles. I laid bizi down an moved through the vehicles. I went back to bizi and allowed him to air scent past the vehicles with a command. Bizi pulled me into a vehicle and searched down the side of it he then flipped around and started to search the vehicle to the left of it and pulled me to the rear of the vehicle and proceeded to crwal up under the vehicle. He stopped at the center under the vehicle and laid down then barked indicating he was on source. The source was hidden in the spare tire

place 2 cotton balls with odor of marijuana on it in a tin can. I placed the source on th passenger side of a deputy car. I took bizi 4 cars away from the source car. I laid him down and did a walk through the search area. I picked him back up and gave him the command to search and started a systimatic search on the first vehicle. We moved through all 4 blank vehicles and when we came to the source vehicle bizi pulle me around the back side of the car and then down the passenger side bizi passed the source but then came back to it quickly sat and stared at the passenger door.

put bizi in his kennel as he has been having anxeity being away from me after my surgery and his. I went to a different room where he could see me and if he scratched or barked I would bump him on a very low setting on the shock collar. For the most part he did well but I did have to give corrections when he barked or scratched.
placed bizi in his kennel and went into another room trying to get him to stop scratching and barking inside the kennel. Bizi did well but had to be corrected a few times over the hour.
placed bizi in a down and used a bite sleeve and let him bite. I then conducted a 3 phase out which he did perfectly and I ended the excersise on the good note.

set up a barrakaed suspect scenerio for the traniees. The purpose of the scenerio is to see if the deputy would use his resources. Once he made contact he discovered that a k9 was need and made the call for one. I placed bizi outside the door and issued warnings. The suspect was highly agitated and was yelling profanities which amped Bizi even further. I released bizi intot he room and he quickly found his target and apprehended him. Myself and the other deputy moved in and placed the suspect in cuffs and then I choked bizi off and took him from the room. Bizi did very well.

still working with bizi on his anxeity in the kennel and not trying to escape or injure himself. I would leave the room while he was locked in the kennel and shock him on a low setting him he scratched or barked inside the kennel. He is doing better inside the kennel I left the home and had my son check on him every 10 mins and he was just aying down the whole time. He never tried to escape.
went for a walk/run with bizi and had him heel to my side this has become a rutine thing and he stays by my side.

continueing trying to get bizi to stay in kennel while im gone without hurting himself. I left thehome and had my wife watch over him if he scrathced or barked she was to bump him on a low setting. Bizi went into the kennel and laid down and waited patiently until I returned home. He is doing lots better in the kennel.

source was placed on a large plow on a high spot. I was given a large area to search it was 4 degrees and the wind was blowing south. I started with a semi truck and when we got to the rear of the truck Bizis head flipped and he pulled me towards a small car I let him move around the vehicle on his own and when he didn’t indicate I took him back to the spot we left off on the truck. Bizi once again pulled away fron the truck and went to the car. He moved around the car and the turned towards the plow and started to move back and fourth it before going on his hind legs then immediately sitting after he was on his hind legs in the center of the plow. I I called the indication and the placer stated that it was the source.

a source was placed on the center of a semi underneath onn the frame. It was 4 degrees and the wind was blowing 2 miles an hour from the north. I started bizi on the front passenger side and moved around past the driver side allowing him to free scent. On the second pass I began presenting areas systematicly. When I got to the rea passenger side bizi tried to get past me and I allowed him to move forward he stopped behind the gas tank and sat and stared. I stated that I would call that indication and the placer stated that I needed to pinpoint. I moved in closer to the vehicle and started to present small areas bizi would sniff then sit he wouldn’t move from the area. I asked how close he was and the placer stated that he was within a couple feet. I tried to get bizi to pinpoint and presented low. He sniffed then went back to where he had indicated he sat then quickly went back to the spot I presented and he sat and indicated on that loaction. I sated I felt he was now on the source and the placer stated that he was.

Pick-up drills with Rocky in the new vest he has. Put him in muzzle as precaution as I could tell he was not exactly sure what was going on. Used the handles on the back of the vest to lift him straight up off the ground and would hold him in place for a couple seconds before putting him back down. After he seemed to be more comfortable. I would pick him up and place him on my shoulders. He seemed okay with this for the most part and did not seem to have any issues with it. Will have to continue working with him to make sure before removing muzzle.

Worked on his bark drill at closed door (door was cracked open slightly.) Would show him pillow and close the door. If he barked I would open the door and allow him to get the pillow. Did this a couple times to enforce the barking at the door.

Took him to outside and tried to do tracking with him with hot dogs in the snow. Did not work very well at all and had to get him back on the track each time. Figured it wasn't working so I moved him to the side of the track a little bit so the wind was blowing towards him slightly. He would move towards the track on his own some but once he got the hot dogs he lost it again. Not sure if tracking in snow is possible, (probably easier to use footprints in snow for tracking purpose and not K9)

Empty house besides myself so I used it to send him in on a building search (dry run) into the house. Placed him in a down at the basement door and called out commands. Had to correct him twice to be quiet. Once he was I sent him in. Allowed him to search and hunt the house until I could tell he was very tired. Praised him up, let him rest and did it a second time sending him in from a different door of the house. He did very well hunting through the house.

After honor guard training, took him cotton balls with odor of marijuana on them. Had family hide them in different places of the house without me knowing where. After letting them cook a little bit, I let him search. First was hidden inside the shoes in the closet near front door. I had to detail the area, but once we got near the shoes I could tell he was in odor as he started to pull towards it. Allowed him to go. He got on odor and sat getting his reward. 2nd was hidden in the floor vent near the couch in living room. Gave him the command to search and allowed a free run through the area first. As we ran by the vent, I noticed the head jerk back towards it. I allowed him to check it on his own, he sat. I called it and was told this was correct. 3rd was hidden in kitchen drawer. Started detailing around cupboards of the kitchen and once he hit odor on the drawer he remained with it and then finally sat. I called this. Was told it was there and I gave him reward.

Worked on his down in motion on the field. He actually did very well so I did not keep going. Wanted to end it on the first very good down in motion. Once he did one without hesitation and without any form of correction. I ended it and allowed him to play with toy some.

RESPONDED TO ASSIST 233 AND 215 WITH THE CALL. WHILE THERE, WAS ABLE TO SEE THROUGH THE REAR WINDOW OF THE VEHICLE AND IT APPEARED THE ENTIRE INSIDE OF THE VEHICLE HAD BEEN TORN APART. ALSO APPEARED TO HAVE SMALL PLASTIC BAGS ON THE FLOOR BOARDS. GOT ROCKY OUT AND RAN HIM AROUND THE VEHICLE. HE SHOWED A LOT OF INTEREST IN THE DRIVERS DOOR BUT NEVER ALERTED ON THE DOOR OR THE VEHICLE. THE TEMP WAS VERY COLD AND COULD HAVE EFFECTED THE ODOR OF ANYTHING INSIDE OF THE VEHICLE. WAS LATER TOLD BY 215 DURING AN INVENTORY OF THE VEHICLE, THEY LOCATED TINFOIL ON THE DRIVER SIDE OF THE VEHICLE NEAR THE DOOR WITH BURNT RESIDUE IN IT. I EXPLAINED THAT WAS PROBABLY WHY ROCKY WAS SHOWING SO MUCH INTEREST BUT NEVER ALERTED BECAUSE HE WAS NOT SURE EXACTLY DUE TO THE VERY COLD TEMPS.

More pick-up drills in the new vest. Lifted him straight up off the ground again using the handles on the back of it. He did well with this. Also placed him over my shoulders again. Still did not do anything. Allowed me to lift him okay.

Placed 4 hides inside the fire station for Rocky to work on finding. All hides were cotton balls with the odor of Scent Logic Heroin on them. The first hide was placed inside an empty "Pre-workout" container which I placed on the concrete pillar between 2 of the garage doors as if someone had simply set it down. When I first entered the area, placed Rocky in a down and did pre-search walk. I gave command to search and allowed him to run through the entire area on his own. He ran by the container and had a slight head jerk on it but continued on. He ran all the way to the front entrance going into the living quarters of the fire station and hit the odor of the hide in there that was placed inside the middle drawer of desk He sat. As I was getting ready to reward him, he stood back up, sniffed that spot again and scratched at it, then went back to a sit. I rewarded him for this. I then took him back into the garage area and began searching around vehicles in there. Rocky alerted on the outside of the truck. I then placed him up inside of it and allowed him to search the inside of it. He was able to hit the odor almost right on. The cotton balls were placed inside the glove box. He was unable to sit but froze in place and stared at the source of the odor. I rewarded him at this point. I then took him to the area of the 3rd hide which was near the washing machine, hide was inside small bag of tide pods. He first passed over the hide but then went back to it. He sat and I gave him his reward. Last hide was the cotton balls inside the pre-workout container. I took him back to the area and began to detail around the firemen gear before moving him over to that area. I then moved to the first garage door and detailed that area go along it. As we went pass the container a second time, I again noticed the head jerk but this time he stayed with it longer. When he moved off it, I spun him around and brought him back. This time he stayed with it and went to an alert. I rewarded him for it.

Worked down and stay. He did very well with this. Rewarded him with treats when he did as told. Also worked on his heeling inside of the house with me.Tried going outside to work the heeling but the snow was too deep for both of us. He did well inside of the house.
Bark drill. He doesn't have any problem with this at all.

Worked him on searching a clean area to see if he would provide any alerts or not simply out of being bored or guessing. He did not alert on anything. Searched several different areas of the house. He never alerted but followed my hand and searched very well

Tatical obedience in the house going from room to room. He did very well with it all. No issues. Rewared with treats when he would either come to me when called or when he stayed where I placed him, left the area and then came back. Did start to whine a little bit at the end when I would go somewhere he couldn't see me.

We did 2 searches today,. First was of an outside container, the second was of the house. First one was inside of the container. Gave commands outside of it, Rocky did well, staying quiet and then going in and searching it. Second was inside of the house. Starting at the back door. Gave him commands and sent him in on a dry run. He did very well searching the house for some time before I ended it bringing it to an end. Praising him up.

Worked on his tatical obedience around the house. Also worked his down and stay and tried working on his heeling. Tatical work went very well, Down and stay was good as well. Heeling was an off day for it. He did not want to heel next to me. So once he started to, I ended the training and put him up after praising him up

Cpl Mathie was on a slide off on i15 and felt the individual he was out with had some very suspcious items in the vehicle. I responded because of the RAS and ran Bizi on the vehicle. Bizi did not alert on the vehicle but because of circumstances I gave the 28 to isp to check the vehcile for it freqency through the area. They have not reported back to me on this issue.

source was placed out in the open under a bucket. I got bizi out for a break and allowed him to be off leash and just wonder the area. Bizi was 10 feet to the west of the source and was walking past it when his head flipped and he moved towards the source. Bizi sat at the bucket then pawed at the bucket.
allowed bizi to bite the sleeve with command. I gave bizi a three phase out which he did so without incident following the commands when given. I ended the excersise and gave him a ball to play with.
placed bizi in his kennel and when he scratched or barked he was corrected. Bizi only barked in the beginning and did well after that. I was out of sight during this excersise.

worked with bizi on his recall and postioning for when he recalls. Bizi returns when given the command very easily. He still likes to move past you on the postion he comes back to you on but is easliy corrected and he will go a full circle around you then settle in on the side told.

was able to take bizi for a walk after not being able to do anything because of covid. On the walk I made bizi stay by my side and heel to my right side while on leash. Bizi does very well at this drill.

while looking for a stolen car for madison county sgt gonzales located the vehicle. During his investigation he discovered that the driver was the owner and madison county had just released it to him. The owner stated he could smell marijuana and wanted his vehicle search by a k9. I responded and could not smell anything. I walked Bizi past the vehcile to get in the starting postion and he pulled me past the front on the vehicle and around the front side of the vehicle. Bizi continued pulling without command and came to the passenger door where he sat. I moved away from him and he stayed on the door and then scratched at the door and barked. I rewarded bizi and pulled him away. Sgt gonzales searched the vehicle and found no source. The owner of the vehicle stated that when the vehicle was found by IF officers the passsenger got out and ran away. It was discovered that the passenger had narcotics on his person.

Bizi was issued a new vest and he is not used to it and is very irritated by it. I put the vest on him and had him heel to my right side as I walked around the building to get him use to the vest. Once he was walking with me and not trying to get out of the vest I did tactical obedience with bizi back around the building. He is still getting use to the vest but he is atleast not trying to rip out of it will continue to work with him on this issue.

I laid bizi ouside the building and I approached. When I got to the door I recalled Bizi and he came to me like always wearing his new vest. We then entered the building and I issued warnings then released bizi into the building to search. Bizi searched the building with no issues while wearing his new vest. I then retrived him and prasied him up there was no suspects hidden it was a dry send.

while doing business check I found an open door at the valley wide. I placed bizi in the rear door and issued warnngs and released bizi into the building. Bizi searched the building and 280 and I followed behind. Nothing was detected inside the building.

Did more bark drills while using the bite pillow. First started out with him on leash and would move towards him when he would bark and then give him the pillow. Then we moved to placing him in a down behind a door. Pillow placed on the other side of the door on the floor. I would give him the command to bark. Once he barked I would open the door and allow him to go in and get the pillow. Moved to making him bark for longer periods before I would open the door for him. No issues except when I would start to open the door he would start to push it open while running in as well. But I do not see down side to this as he is going in to get suspect

Tried to do something a little different today. Worked door pop drills with some obedience added to it. I would place him inside my patrol vehicle and then pop the door using my remote. When he came running out I would have him run over to my location and then go to a down next to me. Would not allow him to do anything else. I would move from one spot to another each time I put him in the vehicle. He did well with coming out of the vehicle and then finding me. Will continue to do more of these.

Noticed the snow in the field next to my residence had melted away some in various spots enough to see the dirt/mud under it in various spots throughout the field. Decided to try some tracking again in this to simulate a muddy or swampy area. Laid a track and let it sit for a short period of time as I was not sure what he would do. Started him on my sent pad I placed and he did well at first following my track (could tell by the footprints in the mud he was following) once we hit the first area that still had snow cover, he lost the track. I allowed him to try and work it on his own to see if he would pick it back up. He did not. I had to put him back on it again on the other side of the snow cover. Then he did well following it again. Seems to loose the scent in the snow. Will talk with Mr. Farley about this and get his thoughts on it.

Another different type of obedience training today. Took him outside and just tossed a toy for him. The only obedience we did today was getting him to come back to me when called, going to a down, and outing the toy when told to do so before I would grab it. It does well with coming back but then wants to run away again. Once he figured out he would get it back, he did better staying and going to a down. And he is getting better at outing the toy when told to do so before I grab it.

Took him to the Ririe Stake Center Pavilion and placed him in a down just on the outside of it. I gave commands as if I was conducting a building search and then sent him in to search the area. It is an open area, but I used it as a building search. If he began to leave the pavilion I would call him back and send him in again. He did very well searching the area.

After we were done at the pavilion, I took him back to my residence and as we were going inside, I placed him in a down and began my commands again. He did whine a little bit but not loud. I sent him in to search the house. He did very well hunting through the rooms and then coming back to me when called.

Worked on his tatical obedience around the outside of the football field area and parking lot area of the school. He did very well and would stay in a down until I either came back to him or called him to me.

Took him to the parking lot of the church to working on his heeling in a different area. He tends to want to pull away from me or rush out in front of me in new areas. So I took him here and used treats to keep him next to me. Once we ran out of treats, I countinued for another 10 minutes to make sure he contiuned to do as before. He did. I praised him up and took him back

Took him outside to the containers again. Gave commands and sent him in to search them. He did very well searching the containers and then moving out of one and going to the other. He jumped back and forth between both of them, searching both for some time before I stopped him and praised him up. Need new places to go.

Took him down below the annex building to work on his heeling again. I did not bring treats or use them this time to see how he would do. He did okay but not as good as I would like him to do. Will work on this more with him without the treats.

Hide was placed inside the wrestling matts near the wall. Rocky hit the odor at the front of the matts from the tube. He sat there waiting for his reward. I tried getting him closer to the source but it seems the odor was being pushed through the tube of the matt and out where he was at at first. He kept going back to it. I rewarded him there as he was not wrong.

Cotton balls with the odor were placed inside the bleachers about half-way up. Rocky was running down the bottom of the bleachers and I noticed the behavior change and could tell he was in odor. He kept going back and forth trying to find the source. I allowed him to work it on his own. He did jump up and began to search higher on his own but sat and alerted a few feet away from the source. I did not reward him and waited to see what he would do. He did not move so I presented the area a little for him getting him closer to the source. Once he hit it. He had a hard sit and again. I rewarded him then.

Cotton balls with odor were placed inside a small hole in the wall in the gym. Rocky was searching the area as I was detailing it. I presented the area about 3 feet below the hide and he got into odor and followed it up. I continued to move away to see what he would do. He stuck his nose right inside and then went to a hard sit. I rewarded him.

Last hide was placed inside of the girls locker room inside locker #57. Before taking him the locker room with the hide, I took him into the boys locker room and had him search that entore area first. He did not alert to anything. I then took him to the girls locker room. He did very well searching, even though I could tell he was getting tired. He continued to search very hard checking everything he could on his own and everything presented to him. Once he got to the area the hide was in, I notced a behavior change and he went straight to the source. And then going to a sit. I rewarded him for that. Praised him up, and put him away after playing with him for some time.

A SEARCH OF A LETTER SUSPECTED OF HAVING POSSIBLE DRUG IN IT WAS CONDUCTED FOR THE JAIL WITH ROCKY. HE DID NOT ALERT ON THE LETTER. HE DID ALERT ON THE BOXER SHORTS INSIDE OF THE PROPERTY ROOM. BUT AFTER LOOKING AT THE VENT INSIDE AND THE DIRECTION IT WAS BLOWING, I BELIEVE IT WAS BLOWING THE ODOR OF AN INMATES CLOTHES THAT DID HAVE METH ON HER TOWARDS THE BOXER SHORTS AND THE ODOR POOLED UP THERE. EVERYTHING WAS 10-4

Worked on his tatical obedience around the high school both inside and outside of it. The first time I placed him in a down and started to walk away, he tried to sneak up on me by slowly walking up, corrected him for this and he never did it again. After that he did as told the entire time. The last couple times, I would hide from him and then recall him using the e-collar tone to see if he would find me. He did find me each time without any problems. Did very well.

Worked on tatical obedience with 225 with us as well. Started out by having 225 move up first then I would move to him. Rocky stayed in a down until called. He did very well, then I switched to me moving first with Rocky staying in a down near 225 (in muzzle) to see what he would do. He stayed in a down until 225 moved to come up, once he did that, he jumped up and moved up with him coming towards me. Will have to work this.

while on a walfare check of a vehicle at a church I discovered the vehicle was empty and found an open door on the church. I brought Bizi to the entrance and issued warnings into the church and released bizi to search. Bizi would move forward but then come back to me. I move forward with him slowly and he would move further forward. Bizi searched the whole building without incident and no one was found.
did recall work with bizi and went for a walk making him heel while he was in his new vest. He is getting use to it and doing well.

placed bizi in a down outside of a room and gave him the command to bark once I was behind it with a bite sleeve. He came at the door and scratched but then barked and I opened the door and let him have the bite after he barked on command.

once it was dark enough I took bizi in the basement of my house with all lights off and made him search he moved very slowly down walls but did search with me in sight. I am going to find a building to make him search while dark to build his confidence.

recall work with bizi as well as kennel work. I did recall work in the back yard bizi is very good at this drill and he comes to my right side and sits or lays. I placed bizi in the kennel and left the room and if he barked or scratch he was corrected. Bizi still not liking the kennel.

source was place on a vehicle in the annex parking lot. Temp outside was -1 degrees and the wind was blowing south at 1 mie an hour. Placed bizi at the beginning of a set of vehicles to search. I walked around the area of the hide and then went back to Bizi and gathered his leash I gave him the command to search and we went around the first vehcile. When we rounded the front of the vehicle bizi pulled me down the driver side of the vehicle and was sniffing with his mouth closed moving down the vehicle. Bizi stopped and sat at the driver side door at the fron crack I released my leash and kept moving backwards and bizi then moved towards me. I gathered his leash back up and then moved to the next vehicle Bizi jerked back towards the first vehicle and kept moving back and forth down it. I gathered his leash and then started a systematic search on the first vehicle. When I came to the front passenger side wheel well Bizi stopp sniffed under the rim and then sat. I dropped my leash and moved away and Bizi stated witht the alert. I told the individual that hid the source id call the location and he gave me the indication that bizi was on source.

placed an agitator in a long hallway with lights on. I walked bizi into the building and gave a warning for the agitatior to come out and he ran I quickly released bizi and he apahended the suspect. I choked bizi off the bite and had the agitator run out of sight while I chased him with bizi. This drill was to give bizi a quick bite as it had been a while since he has done so.

turned lights out and hide agitator in a room. I brought bizi to the front of the building and released him into the dark building giving him the command to apprehend. Bizi search through the building checking doors and until he passed the room the agitator was hiding in. Bizi ran past it flipped around and started to brackket towards the door moving up and down on the wall until he cam to the door. Bizi then stopped at the door stratched the door and then barked. The agitator was instructed to open the door when bizi barked and give him a bite and he did so. I tried a thre phase out with bizi and he didn’t listen to my commands and I had to correct him with the ecollar to come off the bite. When I instructed the agitator to slowly move away bizi reengaged and I had to choke him off. We will be working on three phase out the rest of this week.

on the third bite I placed agitator in the same room and left lights on. I gave warnings and released bizi he went past the door but quickly came back and started barking the agitator opened the door and gave bizi a bite. I let bizi have the bite for a long period and then prasied him and then gave him the command to out and he complyed and released the bite I had the agitatior run out of sight while I chased him and we ended on a good note.

suspect was placed in the upstaires kitchen. Myself and 2 other deputies along with K9 bizi cleared the building moving through it checking doors while Bizi was on leash and in muzzle. Once the suspect was located he was given commands to come out by another deputy or the k9 would be released. I moved to the doorway and issued commands to the suspect to come out or id release the k9 the suspect refused and I released the k9 for a muzzle fight. Bizi did well never shying away from the suspect and engaged continully until I had him hooked up and chased the suspect off.

Had a Jefferson County employee place a hide on their vehicle. When they left the parking lot I made a stop and had all lights activated and mimic a actual stop. I had the driver exit the vehicle and I brought bizi past the driver door and took him to the passenger side front light and laid him down. No hide was placed but I wanted to see if he would alert to anything in a bluff attempt to get his toy or not. I do not want him alerting to something that is not there. On leash heeling in the basement of the annex building. Trying to find different areas to keep working his heeling and get him to stay with me more. Still wants to get out in front of me every time we go to a new area. He did okay but not great.

after an incident at my home bizi was place in his kennel and when he scracthed or barked he was corrected with e collar.

I worked with Bizi on heeling in the back yard off leash while running. He felt like this was playing and keep jumping on me. After a long perid of trial and error he started to kind of get it but still a work in progress.

placed bizi in a down while I walked around my back yard I would return to him if he stayed quite but if he whined or barked I would get further away. worked on Bizis bark drills with the pillow and then used the bite sleeve for 3 phase out. Bizi did well and listend on the 3 phase out on the sleeve this needs to be worked on on the bite suit.

based on RAS built by the state trooper I ran bizi on a vehicle that he had stopped. I brought him to the front of the vehicle on the passenger. did tactical obedience around the building and made bizi sit in one place for 20 minutes. Bizi did well with this. I then called him to me and ran with him while giving him the heel command and he did weel aside from trying to jump on me a few times will keep working on this.

source was hidden in a garbage can at the end of the hall. I brought bizi to the start area which was directly next to the garbage can. I laid him down and did a walk of the search area given to me. During a scenerio for an new deputy a source was hidden in a bathroom up high. I placed bizi outside the bathroom and did a walk through. STOPPED VEHICLE TO ASSIST J6 WITH CITY POLICE ON HIT AND RUN. DRIVER WAS ACTING VERY ODD AND SUSPICIOUS. RAN ROCKY AROUND THE VEHICLE. ROCKY ALERTED TO THE DRIVER DOOR AND WOULD NOT LEAVE IT. Placed the Heroin in the first bottom drawer in the training room at the fire station. 245 told me K9 Bizi did not want to alert to our Heroin and did not know if it was do to the fact it no longer had odor or what. I decided to run Rocky on it at different time frames to see if he would alert. I let it sit for 15 minutes first. I ran Rocky through and he alerted on it. I then moved it to a new location on the other side of the room, placing it under a chair on the floor. I let it sit for 5 minutes and then ran Rocky through the area. He alerted on it again. I moved it to a new loction and let it sit for 45 minutes in the kitchen area just below the fridge. I allowed Rocky to search the area and he located it on his own and alerted to it. Did not have any issues locating the odor and alerting to it. K9 Bizi could have just been not knowing this was it do to it being such a small amount. May need to bring his threashold down some.

On leash heeling while walking him back to the vehicle to put him back in it to continue door pop drills. He again wanted to run out in front of me several times, but after a couple corrections, he would stay by my side better than he has in the past. Might finally be figuring it out.

Hide was inside a plastic baggy inside a plastic evidence bag. Hide was inside a plastic bag and placed in the mens bathroom inside the papertowel roll. Rocky entered the bathroom and began searching it on his own. He hit it and went to a sit staring at it. I rewared him for this.

Hide is inside a plastic bag and placed it inside the fire truck behind the back seat. All window and everything were rolled up on the truck. I brought Rocky around the vehicle doing a detailed search of it as I would any other vehicle. On the first pass around it, I notice he had a change of behavior and a head jerk on the back passenger door but he did not stick with it. We moved on moving around to the front of the vehicle. He then pulled back to the same door he had a head jerk on, sniffing it again. This time he went to an alert on it. I tried getting him to leave it by moving around to the front again but he stayed with it. I then opened up the door and allowed him inside to search. I tried getting him to keep moving with me but he stayed with it. I praised him up and then opened the door and let him inside the vehicle to search it. Again, there was nothing else inside of the vehicle. Used this as "it was there before" type hide. I praised him and then took him back to one of the previous hides from earlier to allow him a win to get his reward.

245 came into the office to get in the bite suit for me to allow Rocky a bite. Started out by hiding him in the mens bathroom in the court hallway. Rocky was sent in to search the area. A bark drill was done. When Rocky barked at the door after locating him in the bathroom, Andrew opened the door allowing him in for the bite. I did a "choke off" and then took him out. I walked him outside and then back in as if we were simply walking down the hallway when suspect runs out of other room. I gave command to stop or I would send the dog. Andrew kept running, Rocky was sent getting him the back. I then did a "3 phase out" to see how he would do on the suit. Rocky came off right away and did not have any issues with this. I had Andrew step away from him, as I walked back up to Andrew. I had Andrew attack me to test Rocky's handler protection. Rocky went in for the bite right away without hesitation. I then outed him by giving him his out command. He came off the bite right away again without any correction. Did a very good job. I had Andrew run away letting Rocky chase him a little bit before stopping him. Praised him up and put him away.

The hide was placed inside the floor outlet in the middle of the room. I took Rocky in the court room and gave him the command to search. I allowed him to search the area on his own to see if he would find it. I could tell he was in odor and was trying to figure out where it was coming from. He kept working it, bracketing along the wall and then floor to the source of the odor. He then went to a down and stare for his alert on it. I gave him his reward.

Hide was placed inside the floor outlet area below the defense attorney desk. After allowing it to sit for some time I took Rocky in and allowed him to search. I could tell he was in odor on the other side of the desk and was trying to figure out where the odor was coming from. I presented under the desk and he was able to locate the source going to a sit and stare.

Placed inside the desk drawer in the hallway. I gave Rocky the command to search. He ran down the hallway on his own. He then worked it around to the front of the desk where he sniffed the drawer and then sat.

Cotton balls with the odor of MDMA were placed inside the boxes of files in the hallway. I gave Rocky the command to search and allowed him a run-by at first to see if he would pick up on the odor. source was placed high on a book shelf. I was instructed of the area it was hidden in and I gave bizi the command to search and he ran down the hallway air scenting then flipped around and went to the book shelf got on his hind legs went high paws on the shelf and sniffed with his head tilted back then sat quickly indicating he was on source. I looked to the individual who hid it for me and he stated he was right under it.

training.Location: jefferson county court house - day off
training.Notes: source was hidden in a breakroom with several plates of food. I gave bizi the command to search and he moved on the outer wall moving towards a cabinet and sat on a drawer. The hidder stated he was on source. Bizi didn’t try to go to the food at all.

training.Location: jefferson county court house- day off
training.Notes: source was hidden on the outside of a room. I gave biz the command to search the room and we moved around it air scenting. Once he had gone around the whole room I did a systimatic search and I came to the other dor and presented the cracks and bizi sniffed hard on the cracks then laid down with his nose at the bottom of the door indicating he was on odor.

training.Location: jefferson county court house- off duty
training.Notes: source was hidden in a bottom desk drawer I released bizi intot he room air scenting. Bizi went sright to the desk and started to scratch at the drawers. Bizi than sat and barked indicating he was in odor.

Hide was 2 cotton rounds placed on the board near the front desk higher up. Rocky was alerting to the source on the other side of the door before we entered the search area. Once in the search area, he kept alerting to the corner or the room. Had to present the hide to him in to get him on it. Later noticed the vent was blowing the odor directly towards the area he was alerting.

Hide was a sticker that was placed under a table near the wall. Rocky got into odor of it at the front of the table and began to bracket the odor towards the source. I called up under the table at first and was told to pin-point as he was very close. I allowe him to work it more and he went further back towards the back of the table before going to an alert again. I called the back of the table which was correct. Reward was given

Hide was placed inside of the break room area in the bottom drawer of the stove. I allowed Rocky to enter the room to began searching on his own as it is a smaller room. As he entered, he went straight to the source and alerted on the drawer. I called this and was told this was correct. Reward was given

Hide was placed in a drawer below some plants. This was the last find for Rocky and he was very tired with his tounge hanging out. I began the search by detailing the area to try and help him. I noticed he kept closing his mouth on the drawer and kept going back to it on his own so I allowed hi to keep working it. He finally went to an alert. I called the drawer and was told this was correct. Reward was given. I praised him a lot and put him back in the vehicle to allow him to rest.

Worked on-leash heeling outside in the parking lot. At first he wanted to take off out in front of me like he normally does but I would correct him with his fur saver collar and redirect him. After a few corrections he started to stay next to me. Once we moved from the parking lot to inside of the building, walking down the court hallways, he went right back to wanting to go out in front of me pulling again. Not sure why he will not stay in heel.

Worked on-leash heeling more up and down the hallways again. Also spent some time going through different areas of Annex building as well. He again wants to pull out in front of me the second we enter a new area. Had to correct him a lot on fur saver and redirect him, to get him to stay with me. Once he started doing well, I would enter a new area and we would have to start all over again. I got him outside and continued this until he was walking beside me without needing any corrections. I then praised him up a lot and ended the training.

245 came in to get in the suit to work some bite work with Rocky. We went to Central Fire and Andrew got inside of the mobile command unit in the bay. After being inside for around 20 minutes, I brought Rocky in to conduct a building search. I placed him in a down and began giving my commands. Rocky began barking and wanting to just go out on his own. I had to tell him several times to remain quiet and correct him back to a down. I tried giving my commands in a quieter tone to see if that would help but he continued to whine. Once he stopped whining I sent him to search. He searched the area running into the other bay as well. Then coming back. Once he got between the command unit and fire truck I could tell he was in odor and he was trying to figure out where from. He finally went inside the command unit locating Andrew and getting the bite. I did a choke off and pulled him out as Andrew hide inside.

After getting Rocky away from the command unit, I had Andrew run out of it. I sent Rocky after him and tried getting him to do a "down in motion" this was a very short distance for him and he did not do it. I decided to do a "3 phase out" as the call off. Rocky did do as commanded but not as fast as he did last week. As I began to walk towards him to get his leash, he took off after Andrew again, going in for a bite again. I again did a "3 phase out" for the call off. He did not want to let go right away from what I could see but Andrew said he could tell Rocky had a tooth stuck inside of the suit but was trying to let go. Again, as I was walking towards him, he again took off re-engaging in the bite again. I called him off again and this time He remained in a down until I was able to get the leash and dismiss Andrew from the area. I praised him up and put him back in my vehicle.

Worked his heeling again while on-leash. Once again same issues as before, once we get to a new area, he wants to pull out in front and start working the area. He is all go and no waiting for him ever. Will maybe try and use hotdogs or dog treats with him for this to see how he does with that instead of not using anything at all.

Did a door pop drill while I was at the corner of the church bizi came out found me and then laid by my side to get ready to advance. Will keep working this drill.

tactical obedience with bizi on my right side we tactically advance with a rifle on my shoulder and did tactical obedience.
