Did a door pop drill while I was at the corner of my house bizi came out found me and then laid by my side to get ready to advance. Will keep working this drill.

placed bizi in a down and walked out of sight after 10 mins I returned and gave him a treat. I walked out of sight once again waitied 20 mintues returned and rewarded bizi he stayed in the down the whole time.

hid in different parts of the park and popped the door. Bizi came out and searched around for a while until he saw me then ran to me. On the second try I stood out by the church and popped the door. Bizi got out and ran towards the opposite side of the building until he saw me then changed up and ran towards me.

source was placed in with a bunch of files up high in a filing room. I let bizi into the room and search it without command. Bizi moved around the room sniffing high and moving back and fourth across the wall that the source was hidden on. He then tilted his head clear back and went up on his hind legs and placed his front feet on the wall. He than quickly sat and barked alreting below the source. I pulled on his leash to see if he would come away from the source and he pulled back and maintained his seated postion.

placed the suspect in a pitch dark room and placed him behind a curtin. I released bizi into the room once warnings were given and bizi went in and without hesitation went in and found the suspect. Once bizi was on the bite I attempted a three phase out and bizi listened to me and released on the first attempt.

conducted a traffic stop. Once the drive was out of the vehicle he started to fight with me. I could hear bizi barking while I was fighting. I door popped bizi and he came in and assited with the apprahension of the suspect without issues. Once the suspect was down I outed bizi with a command and he listened on the first try.

Hide was placed inside the mens bathroom in locker #8. Was Meth that had been found inside of the jail. Let it sit and cook for an hour and then sent Rocky in from the bathroom door going into the bathroom. He went straight to the source without going anywhere else. Hit the locker and went to a sit right away. Reward was given.

JAIL THOUGHT THEY HAD FOUND SOME NARCOTICS IN THE MAIL. REQUESTED ROCKY COME IN AND DO A SNIFF TO SEE IF HE WOULD ALERT TO IT AT ALL OR NOT. BROUGHT HIM IN AND HAD HIM SNIFF THE MAIL THAT WAS PLACED ON THE FLOOR. HE DID NOT ALERT TO IT. TOOK HIM OUT AND TOOK HIM TO A KNOWN HIDE TO REWARD HIM ON. EVERYTHING WAS 10-4

Placed cotton balls with odor on them inside the back corner of the pavilion of the stake center. I let them sit and cook there for a little over an hour and then sent Rocky from the parking lot area to search. I allowed him to run around on his own searching and noticed as he got closer to the pavilion he got in odor and began to follow it. Once inside, the wind blowing it around made it a little more difficult for him to locate and we had to begin doing more of a detailed search of the area before he was able to pin-point it more. Once he got to it, he located it and went to a sit and stare alert.

Worked on his bark drill using the bite pillow again. Same as before, would let him see me toss it into a room. I would then close the door and tell him to go get it. He would not get the door opened for him until he began to bark at it. The last one I did not let him see where it was and I placed it behind the door and let it sit for a little while. I then gave him the command and he went hunting. He Located the scent of the pillow at the base of the door and began to bark. I opened the door and let him get it.

Worked on his heeling with the leash at the house. Once again, while at home he has no issues staying in a heel with me. It's anytime we get anywhere else he wants to bolt out in front and do his own thing.

throughout the day I worked with bizi going through closed doors while he was heeling on my right side. Bizi tried to blast through a few of the first doors but after we kept doing the drill he would look up at me before entering. This was a good dril will keep working on this.

throughout the day I worked on tactical obedience and tactical advance while I held a rifle. The tactical obedience Bizi is fimilar with this drill and did well didn’t break. On the tactical advance bizi likes to try and get in front of me while moving forward. At one point he jumped up at my rifle. Will keep working this drill.

in two different session I placed bizi in the patrol car and went into my back yard still having a visual. I door popped bizis door remotly and he came out looking for me. He found me very quickly and was rewarded with the ball.

while doing tasks around the house I tethered bizi to me with a leash and made him stay on my right side. Bizi is fimiliar with this drill and in the beginning he doesn’t like it but after time he does well.

was called out to assist Isp on a stop. Bizi tried pulling me to the vehicle before we were able to start when we started his head jerked back towards a door we passed but kept moving forward when we came back to the door bizi got on his hind legs and sniff a cracked window. He than sat and barked but I took some steps away and he followed but quickly pulled back to the spot and sat and barked and then began scratching.

had a deputy hide a source outside on a vehicle. When I got to the area I was shown an area with two vehicles. I started on the furthest vehicle and made a pass and did a systimatic search on the first vehicle which biz did not alert on. I moved to the 2nd vehicle and while passing the front of the vehicle bizi tried to push past me and went to the crack between the cab and the bed of the vehicle. Bizi got on his hind legs and then sat and barked. The deputy that placed the source stated the source was just up under the lip of the bed wall right where bizi was alerting.
tactical obedience around the building. Aside from bizi whining while im away from him he does well and doesn’t break.

Upon arrival, I removed K9 Bizi from my patrol vehicle and took him straight to the front passenger side of the suspect vehicle. When I got Bizi to the starting point, he sat down, and I observed his head tilt back. Bizi put his nose in the air, moved his head back and forth, and then broke his starting point towards the vehicle. I told Bizi to get back in the starting position, and when I did so, he sat down close to the vehicle. I gave him the command to search, and we moved across the front of the vehicle and past the driver's door. Bizi then pulled me around to the passenger side, and he moved closely down the side with his nose close to the vehicle. He passed the passenger door and then quickly turned around and went back to the front passenger door and sat immediately, indicating that he was in the odor of narcotics. I pulled on Bizi's leash, and he barked and scratched at the vehicle alerting further that he was in the odor of narcotics. I pulled Bizi away, praising him, and put him back in my vehicle
took bizi through several vehicle with no hides on them. Bizi didn’t pull or alert on any of the blank vehicles.

Worked on his "down-in-motion" where the snow has melted enough to do so on the field in the area. Rocky did not want to go down when told to do so. Tried correcting him on the e-collar each time going up one level higher every time. He would continue to run through it to get the ball. Had e-collar maxed out on correction level and he continued to run through the corection until he got the ball. Once he had it, he would do what he was told then. Continued working him, letting him run more and more but not corecting him. I wanted to tire him out before trying again. Only threw the ball for him. Then when I could tell he was very tired, I then began to give commands to go down again. The first couple he ran through the correction again. The last 3 times, he did exactly as he was told, going to a down before getting the ball. Did not have to correct him on the very last one. So once he went down without a correction. I let him get the toy, praised him (Huge) played with him a little bit longer, then put him up ending the training to end on a good note.

Worked on his "down-in-motion" again today. He wanted to do the same as yesterday and run through the command. I began to correct him on the e-collar and he continued to run through a level 4 until he got the ball. Once he had it, I called him back to me, and when I throw it a second time, he went to a down when told. I praised him and rewarded him with the other ball. Third throw he ran through the command and correction again until he had the ball, on the fourth throw, he went down on the command. It seemed every second time he would anticipate what was coming and do it. So the last couple times I did not give him the command, when he went to a down, I told him to keep going to get the ball. Then the last time, when I felt he was not anticipating the command anymore. I told him to go to a down. He did as told. I rewarded him with the other ball, praised him up and ended the training.

Used the bite sleeve and let Rocky bite it on the floor. After letting him get it, I would ppick it up and then give him the commands for "3 phase out" he did very well letting go each time on the first or second command. I would then let him take the sleeve again and start over. We did this several times.

Jackie got in the suit near the Sheriffs office door. I brought Rocky out of the patrol office and while controlling him with his vest, I placed him in a bite on the suit. He did very well maintaining a constant bite the entire time, and went to a deeper bite on his own several times while I praised him up. I then after letting him pull her around some, did a "choke off" while she ran away from him into the other room allowing him to chase her a little bit and then took him outside to let him rest.

Had Rocky in a down in the hallway near the Sgt's office in muzzle, 240 brought the bite sleeve and bite suit top out into the hallway. Rocky went after them trying to get them through the muzzle. I allowed him to try for a few seconds before putting him back in a down near the items and then removing the muzzle. I then kept him in a down near them not letting him get them. Each time he tried to break to get them, I would correct him and place him back in a down. After he stayed in a down for several minutes without having to be corrected, I allowed him to get what he wanted as his reward. I then prasied him up, played with him some, then took it from him and put him in the patrol him to rest.

Worked on off leash obedience just to give it a try. Used the E-collar as form of correction for when he got to far out in front of me. Did not say anything when he did, I would stop in place, and give him a zap to get his attention, he would come back and sit next to me. Then we would start again. Not sure how well it really worked for him, but towards then end, he never got too far out in front.

Worked on down in motion using balls. The first time he ran through the command to go down and went to the ball. On the second try he was anticipating the command some but did go down when told to go down. Rewarded him with another ball and then played with him throwing the balls for him for some time. Tried doing a down in motion again during this and he did go down when told to do so. Rewarded him again and continued playing with him and then ended the training on this

WAS ASKED BY ISP TO SEARCH TRUCK AND TRAILER WITH ROCKY. ROCKY ALERTED ON THE POWER UNIT ON THE PASSENGER SIDE OF THE VEHICLE SEVERAL TIMES. SEARCHING INSIDE AND OUT WAS UNABLE TO LOCATE ANYTHING. PASSENGER STATED HIM AND DRIVER HAVE BEEN AROUND PEOPLE USING MARIJUANA AND COULD POSSIBLY HAVE ODOR ON CLOTHING

Worked on his down in motion again along with door pop drills. He did very well with the door pop drills with running up to me and going to a sit or down (depending on the command I gave him) and then I would reward him with throwing his toy out for him to go get. I then brought in the down in motion and would throw the toy as he was running up to me and then tell him to go to a down. The first couple times he would run through the command and correction to get the ball, then he started doing what he was told. After he finally went to a down fast and did as he was told. I recalled him back to me and put him away without letting him go get the ball. Ending on a high note.

Laid a track through the field near the church now that the snow has melted. Only laid it from one side of the field to the other was all and let it sit for a little while before running him on it. He did better than I thought he would after not working a track for so long. He did his normal zig zag over the top of the track but stayed on it for the most part. He only came off the track twice but did not get very far off it before coming back to it. Will continue to work these more with him again.

Did a buried hide out in the yard with him today to see how he would do. Hide wasn't fully buried but enough he would not see it right away. Cotton balls with the odor on them placed under inside a small altoids can that was then placed under a pile of dead grass outside. I let him search, trying to get him to search in a "grid" pattern but he wanted to just kind of run around on his own, kept him near me, presenting the "pattern" and he eventually came upon the hide and alerted to it. Has a slower sit, that needs to be worked on again. Rewarded him for his alert.

placed bizi in a down outisde a doorway. I went into the room without saying anything to him. I sat out of his sight and after 15 minutes he broke and came looking for me. I took him further out side the doorway and did the same thing and he broke after 10 minutes. I did so again even furthher away from the doorway and after 10 mins I went to him gave him a treat and then went back and waited again and did this every 10 to 15 minutes. Without the treats bizi broke. We wil work on this.

placed bizi in muzzle and layed him down. I threw a soccor ball down the yard and once it landed I released bizi to get the ball and let him play with the ball. The first few gos bizi broke and went for the ball before I gve commands. I let the ball land and made him sit longer than usual then released him and made him push the ball around with the muzzle. After he was doing well on waitng for the command I threw an old basketball and took the muzzle off and let him tear it up. Excersise is to help with his muzzle fighting and drive to bite.

took bizi for a run. The first mile he did well and stayed by my side heeling. After the first mile he got frustrated and kept pulling in front of me. I havent ever took him on that long of a run without a tracking. Next time im going to take treats.
throught out the day I made bizi heel to my side and I would move forward slowly while holding rifle down range and make him stay by my side slowly. He is getting use to this excersise and does well.

paparing biz for my trip away from him I placed him in kennelfor most the day and if he barked scratched or tried to get out I would correct him with the e collar. Bizi still hates the kennel at home and trys to get out. When at work the car kennel he does well it is only the home kennel.

while havng the k9 on long line I had a 3rd party throw a toy out of sight and slowly let bizi out laying him down every 5 feet. Bizi did not like this he tried to pull t go get the toy. tried to do a long line search again letting him out slowly and got a little better but had to use corrections still.
played with biz just simple recall work with a ball and a toy. His recall is grat and he heels to my right side when he returns

throughout the day I would down bizi and hide a toy and tell him to search I wuld let him just try and find it and see how long he would try. His drive to hunt is high and he searched until he found it twice.

search for probation and parole. On my way in with K9 Bizi, I walked him past Taylor's vehicle and took a pass around it, and he did not indicate on the vehicle. I took Bizi into the home and gave him the command to search, and he tilted his head back and was sniffing high as he moved through the home. Bizi moved back towards the front door but then moved towards the wall that the cabinet was on that the substance was located in and sniffed high and moved down the wall. Bizi passed under the cabinet where the substance was and went further into the home but turned around and came back towards the area. He moved down the wall sniffing low and high, went into the back bedroom, moved around the bed, sniffed all the drawers and cabinets in the room, then moved out of the room, going back towards the area it was located. Bizi got in the area and kept moving back and forth, trying to get close to the source. I could tell he was in odor by the way he was sniffing high, but he couldn't get close enough. I lifted Bizi on a chair where he could get closer, and he sniffed and stared at the cabinet. Bizi jumped off the chair, stared straight up at the cabinet, and sat and barked. I took Bizi out of the trailer and put him away. After bizi was put away taylor told me that she had just smoked meth in the home and that would explain why bizis head was tilted back during the whole search the odor was stronfg in the whole home.

had a deputy hide a source on a vehilce in the parking lot. The source sat for 4 hours and it was 36 degrees. The wind was blowing 3 mph. I started bizi on the front passenger side and moved towards the driver side. I started with a systematic search and moved down the driver side I crossed the back side of the vehicle and went past the passenger rear wheel. As we passed the rear whell bizi snapped back went to the wheel and stopped and stared at the wheel then went to a sit. I called the hide and the deputy confirmed it was the hide

using the long line I released bizi to the entrance. From approximately 15 feet away from the entrance I laid him down at the door while I stayed back. I gave my comands loudly into the building from that distance. Bizi stayed quite and didn’t break his down until I released him. Once bizi was released the team moved forward and I tried to lay bizi downin the hall way close to the first two doors. Bizi laid down but then came bac to me. I sent him again and he tried to blast into the building to search I tried to stop him at the doors again and he returned to me. The team moved forward and I releaed bizi into the rooms to search. We continued our search this way until the building was cleared. Having bizi check doors like I was trying to get him to do will take some time.

deputy mcrae was apprached by an indivdual that was reporting strange things and while he was speaking with him he felt that the indivdual was intoxicated by narcotics. I arrived and spoke breifly with the individual and asked for consent to run bizi on his vehicle and he consented. I started bizi on the fron passenger side and let him aior scent the vehicle on the first pass. On the second pass I started a systimatic search and only made it to the front crack of the driver door before bizi pt his nose on the vehicle and took a deep sniff and than sat down and staared at the crack. I dropped my leash and took several steps back and bizi stayed at the place he sat and continued staring. I praised him away and searched the vehicle finding shake marijuana in a container right by the crack.

another deputy placed a sticker that had been in with meth on a wheel. I got busy and wasn’t able to run the search so it sat for 48 hours. Once I started the search I took bizi to the front of the vehicle and started him on the passenger side. I started with a systimatic search and made a pass around the vehicle and while doinf so bizi would pull back and run the other direction then start back going the other way but he would tilt his head back and I coulld tell he was in odor. I started the second pass and we passed the driver door and bizi pull back tt he front of the vehicle then put his nose to the vehicle then moved back towards the rear then switched and went back towards the front he went to the front wheel where the source was and put his nose on it and laid down and stared.

Worked on his heeling again. After speaking with Ricky Farley at K9 Conference, he suggested getting a pinch collar to tryand use that. I am waiting for it to arrive. I used regular fur saver collar, and just worked on his obedience with heeling outside before coming to work. He did very well with staying next to me, but always does when we are at the house. Just wanted to make sure he understood what it is I am wanting him to do once the pinch collar gets here.

Used the e-collar on the lowest setting of a lvl 1. Worked on Rocky not just jumping right out of the car when I open the door every time. I also worked on him going back and getting back in the vehicle on his own when told do so. At first he fought me on everything as it was new to him. I helped him understand what it was I was wanting him to do. Outside of the vehicle, when I would tell him to go get back in, I would tap the e-collar button until he got inside of the vehicle. Once he was in, I stopped. If he came out at all, I started tapping the button again, telling him to get back in, and would not stop until he got back in. He got the idea of the game and then when he went straight to the vehicle and got in, without me having to tap the button at all. I praised him up big time, and ended the drill.

Hide was 4 cotton balls placed in the top drawer of a file cabinet in what I believe was a training room at the fire station. When we first entered the room, I could tell he was already in odor but I started out by doing a detained search working our way around the room. I was also working on his sit when coming upon source of odor trying to get him to go back to that faster sit. He presented high on the file cabinet and he was right on the odor. Toy was inside with the hide. As he was coming down, I used my leash and smacked him on his butt a little bit getting him to go to a faster sit than his normal "hydrolic sit" Once he was sitting, I slowly opened the drawer, and reached in and made his toy come shooting out the top of it.

Hide was 3 cotton balls placed in the bottom drawer of the desk in captains office. When I took Rocky in. I placed him in a down at the door going into the office. I then walked around the room, and then came back to him. I gave him the command to search and he ran straight to the desk. He sniffed the drawers, but was trying to move so quickly he moved away from the source where hide was at but then turned around and came back to it with a head jerk. He then started searching the desk area again on his own. I allowed him to search it and his finally alerted on the desk just on the oppiste side of where the hide was placed. I noticed air flow was blowing the odor that direction so I spun him around and began to detail down the wall working towards the desk. I wanted to place his nose directly on the hide. Once I did, he took a deep sniff in and I used leash to smack him on the butt a little bit getting him to sit faster. Once he did, I use slight of hand to reward him.

Placed the entire contaier of odor inside of the microwave in the station. Microwave was closed up. I had Rocky do a detailed search working our way around the room searching down the walls first, then moving towards the microwave. I could tell the closer we got to it, the more "in odor" he was getting. He kept moving faster and faster, trying to get to it as we went. Once we got there. He sniffed the microwave and then sat pretty quickly on his own. Used slight of hand to reward him.

Hide was the entire pouch of Scentlogic odor placed inside of the glove box of the light truck (#153) in the bay area of the station. I began the search by having Rocky search around the other vehicle next to it first, then working our way to the one with the hide on the inside of it. Rocky alerted to the passenger side of the vehicle. Going to a sit. I then opened the door and placed him inside. I allowed him to search the cab of the vehicle until he was able to locate the source. He froze in place (could not sit, no room to do so) and starred at source. I rewarded him at this point.
took bizi for a walk and had him heel the whole time. After we returned I put him outside my doorway and went in making him wait for me to return. Bizi stayed in the doorway and didn’t break.

This was a buried hide. I placed the entire container inside a springler box near the south/west side of the building. I placed the lid back on top of it and it was flush with the grass on the ground. Hide was acutally another foot below. Rocky was given the command to search on his own. I just wanted to see what he was doing. Wind was blowing with a slight breeze going to the north. Rocky came in from the south. He kept going to the side of the building which was nothing but a break wall. Odor must have been going that way with the wind, even though it was blowing the other direction. . I pulled K9 Bizi from my vehicle, brought him to the front passenger side of the vehicle, and laid Bizi down about 5 feet away from the front bumper. Bizi quickly crawled to the bumper and tilted his head backward, indicating he was in an odor. I gave Bizi the command to search and let him air scent the vehicle. Bizi moved across the front of the vehicle and went to the driver's door. Bizi moved back and forth on the driver's door but continued. We went all the way around the vehicle, and I started a systematic search at the passenger bumper. I got Bizi going in an up and down motion around the vehicle. We made a pass, and Bizi slowed and went back and forth on the door when we came to the passenger door. I moved on, and Bizi came with me, and we started our final pass. We came to the driver's door, and as we kept moving, Bizi pulled back towards the front of the vehicle then, sniffed the front door crack and then went up on his hind legs, and then moved to the crack on the front door opening, and he sat and stared at the door. I pulled on Bizi's leash, and he didn't move. He kept staring at the door, indicating that he was in the odor of narcotics. I dropped his leash and took several steps away from him, and Bizi stayed staring at the door and didn't move. I went back to him, praised him, and took him to my vehicle. Meth and marjijuana were found later in a search.

ASSISTED REXBURG PD, AND ST. ANTHONY PD WITH SEARCHING THE ST. ANTHONY WORK CAMP AT THEIR REQUEST. DURING THIS TIME ROCKY AND I SEARCHED 6 DORM ROOM AREAS. EACH ROOM HAD 16 BUNKS IN THEM. ROCKY DID REALLY WELL SEARCHING AND NOT GIVING UP ON HIS SEARCH. WHEN HE STARTED TO GET TIRED I GAVE HIM A BREAK FOR 15 MINUTES AND THEN STARTED AGAIN. ROCKY ALERTED IN ONE ROOM IN "ECHO DORM" TO A SMALL BUNK LOCKER. INSIDE OF THE LOCKER A SMALL AMOUNT OF MARIJUANA WAS LOCATED. THEN I TOOK HIM INSIDE THE BATHROOM AREA WHERE HE ALERTED ON THE TOILET PAPER DISPENSER IN THE MIDDLE STALL, AND THEN ALERTED ON THE TOILET ITSELF IN THE HANDICAP STALL. I brought Bizi past Sean's vehicle on the driver's side, and as we walked by, Bizi turned and pulled towards Sean's vehicle. I continued to move, and Bizi moved with me, and I brought him to the front passenger side of the vehicle and laid him down. As soon as Bizi was laid down, he got up, moved closer to the vehicle, and I laid him down again. Bizi, now within a foot away from the vehicle with his head tilted back, indicating he was in the odor of narcotics, I gave him the command to search. Bizi got to the driver's side door on the first pass, tilted his head upwards close to his mouth, and took a big breath in but continued to move. We made it around the backside of the vehicle and to the passenger side, where Bizi closed his mouth and took a deep breath on each crack as we moved around the front of the vehicle. I then started a systematic search with Bizi going up and down pattern. As soon as we got to the driver's door, Bizi closed his mouth, looked up, and then got on his hind legs and tried to sniff up at the top of the window. He came down onto all fours, went to the crack at the front of the vehicle, sat and barked, and then started scratching at the vehicle. I tried to get him to stop scratching, so he moved to where the driver's door would open, sniffed with his mouth closed, and then sat and barked, indicating he was in the odor of narcotics. I stepped away from Bizi and tugged on his leash, and he wouldn't move from his indication. I praised Bizi and put him away. Paraphernilia and marijuana were found.

The home was located approximately one hundred yards to the east of the intersection of 9th street and Oxford drive, where a command post had been set up. The home we were going to be moving towards, front door was facing south and was on the north side of 9th street. With my lethal attachment, he and I moved forward towards the home. When we got about fifty feet away, we were directed to go to the west side of the house. A team of six swat members had posted up to enter a doorway on the west side of the house. Once we met up with the team, I moved into the stack's third position, and the team moved further east through a fence and alongside the west side of the house. The point man moved to the north side of the doorway and made sure it was safe for Bizi and I to approach. I moved into the second position and placed Bizi in the doorway. 

I issued three warnings into the home and warned any occupants they could be bitten if they didn't comply and exit the home. Along with my warnings, Idaho Falls Swat issued further warnings over a loudspeaker, warning that noncompliance could end in getting bit. Once the warnings were issued, I gave Bizi the command to apprehend and released him into the home. Bizi first ran in and then exited quickly, I motioned towards the doorway and issued the apprehend command again, and Bizi ran in and then exited quickly again. On the third send, Bizi entered, moved around, and came to the exit. Bizi stayed in the home but stayed at the doorway and barked. I removed my gas mask so Bizi could see my face laid him down, then reissued the command, and he moved into the home searching. Bizi came back to the doorway and sat at the door, which had a set of stairs that I couldn't see. The point man informed me that he was positioned at the top of the stairs and wasn't moving. I looked to the member directly behind me and told him Bizi was indicating on something, and we pulled Bizi out of the home to regroup and strategize for the entry into the home. 

Myself and Bizi and my lethal attachment stayed on the west side of the home on the outside while ten swat members moved into the home and posted up where Bizi had already cleared. Once they got to their position, Bizi and I reentered the home, went into the living room area, and I pointed Bizi down a hallway with three doors. Bizi went into each room, searching intently before exiting and returning to the living room. Bizi jumped up on the couch and barked. I asked if there were narcotics in the open that could be seen where Bizi was, and I heard one of the members say yes. I pulled Bizi away from where he was. Bizi quickly went back down the hall and into a room where I could see insulation on the floor from an attic. When Bizi entered this room, he kept looking up towards the ceiling area and would leave but go back in and lookup. I told the swat members what I saw from Bizi, and I pulled him out so they could get additional tools to assist with clearing the attic. I told the officer in charge of the operation inside the home that we could place Bizi on the shield and lift him into the attic if we had a ballistics shield. The officer quickly commanded one of the other members to get the shield while we prepared to move into the room. The decision was made to set off another round of gas, and Bizi and I exited the home for the deployment of the gas. 

Once the gas had been deployed, we reentered and went to the room at the end of the hallway. Once in the room, swat members used specialized tools to look into the attic, and they saw some blankets and other clothing in a corner. Swat members then issued warnings into the attic stating that a K9 would be put in the attic, and if they didn't comply, they could be bit. We prepped to deploy Bizi into the attic when there was no answer by bringing in a step ladder and the ballistics shield. I laid Bizi down on the shield, and two swat team members assisted me in lifting Bizi into position to get into the attic. I got on the step ladder and directed Bizi into the attic. Bizi was unsure what to do, and I had to assist him further by pushing him up. Bizi jumped into the attic, stayed on the ledge close to the opening, and then jumped back down on the shield. Once Bizi did this, the decision was made to bring him down and use other options to clear the attic.

While en route, I was informed that at a quick glance through the passenger window, there was folded-up tinfoil noticed on the floorboard. With my training and experience, I know it could be used for the use of drug-related offenses. With this knowledge, I had reasonable articulable suspicion to believe there were narcotics located in the vehicle. Upon arrival, I deployed K9 Bizi from my vehicle and took him to the front passenger side of the vehicle, a white Chevy pickup four-door, and laid him down. When I laid Bizi down, he immediately moved closer to the bumper of the vehicle and then started pulling towards the driver's side. The wind was blowing east towards the driver's side of the vehicle, and it was blowing through the vehicle from the west with its windows down. I circled him around, laid him back down in front of the passenger side light, and then gave him the command to search. On the first pass, I gave Bizi a chance to free air sent the vehicle, and when we got to the driver's side rear, Bizi pulled away and started going towards a large electrical box in the grass east of the vehicle. Bizi sniffed around it for a second and then returned to the vehicle. I was later informed that right where Bizi was sniffing. The female passenger had gotten out of the vehicle and sat next to the box. When Bizi returned to the vehicle, we continued the free air sniff to the passenger front bumper. I started to systematically search the vehicle when Bizi pulled back, went in front of the vehicle and back to the passenger door, and went back and forth from the rear passenger door to the front passenger door. He then got on his hind legs and went up the crack that joined the two doors. I noted where Bizi was interested and then continued my systematic search. We made it to the driver's door before Bizi again pulled back, went in front of the vehicle back to the passenger door, sniffed the bottom crack, and then quickly sat and stared at the door crack. I moved away from Bizi and pulled on his leash for him to come with me, and he pulled back and stared back at the vehicle and would not move from his seated position. I praised Bizi and returned him to my patrol vehicle. Several sources found.
