I had Lieutenant Clements take each baggie and put them in their own packages and then took three empty boxes out into the sallyport, where I placed them all apart with only one box containing the items in the black trash bags. On the first search, the coffee grounds were in a small box, and I brought Bizi in, walked through the boxes, and then gave the command to search. We moved around each box with Bizi not showing any mannerisms or changing his actions towards any of the boxes.

The second was the baggy of punch placed in its own box with three boxes containing nothing. I brought Bizi in and laid him down, and he immediately broke his down went to the box with the punch in it and started barking. I moved away from him. I called for him to come to another box, which he did, then quickly turned around, went back to the box with a punch, and lay down. I continued walking backward away from Bizi, walked around a van outside of Bizi's view, and stayed there for several seconds. I then came out, walked past Bizi, walked out of the sallyport, and stood outside. Bizi never broke away from the box containing the baggie of punch. I took the box with the baggie of punch, moved it to another section in the sallyport underneath one of the jail vehicles, placed the baggie of sugar in its own box, and brought Bizi back in.

I gave Bizi the command to search, took him off leash, and let him search the sallyport independently. Bizi moved around the boxes we had placed out, including the box with the bag of sugar, and he showed no interest. Bizi went to the far west corner between two jail vans, where I saw him tilt his bed head back, look to the sky, turn around, and came running back towards the back of the van. He then ran past the back of the vehicle where the box was placed, turned around, went to the passenger rear door, crawled underneath the vehicle where the box was laying, and pushed it further up underneath the vehicle. When doing so, Bizi got up, went to the vehicle's rear, and then sat, indicating that he was in the odor of narcotics. Bag sent to lab

Upon arrival, I was informed that the substance came from the trailer so they could also detect the odor of marijuana but wanted the K9 to try and pinpoint it. I brought Bizi up to the front of the motorhome, laid him down, and walked around it, looking for any dangers. I returned to Bizi, gave him the command to search, and we moved across the front of the vehicle to the driver's side and then down towards the rear of the driver's side. When we reached the rear, Bizi pulled back, went to the center of the motorhome, and tried crawling underneath it to get to the odor he was detecting. When Bizi couldn't crawl under any further, he came out, came back to me, and we continued around the backside and up the passenger side. Once we came to the motorhome door, Bizi put his nose to the door and quickly came to a sit indicating that he was in the order of narcotics. I rewarded Bizi and returned him to my patrol vehicle. Several sources found.

Hide was 4 cotton balls with the odor placed inside of a hand sanitizer dispenser in the hallway. This was the last hide Rocky was trying to find. I began by detailing a section of lockers on the other side of the hall. I then spun to the other side detailing the chairs and benches. When we got to the hide he alerted to it fast going to a sit. I rewarded him for this.

Hide was the entire pouch of MDMA that was placed inside a rolled up wrestling mat. Rocky first ran past this hide even though he was in odor before given the command to search. He ran past it to the second hide that was in a locker. He then came back after being rewarded on the second one and worked his way around the mat to the source of where the odor was coming from the strongest. He went to an alert of lying down in front of it where I rewarded him for this.

Hide was cotton balls placed inside of locker # 240. This was the second hide Rocky was supposed to look for but instead ran past the first one straight to this one. He located this hide on his own going to a hard sit right away. As I was walking down the hall to him, he would jump up and scratch at the locker then come back down to a sit and stare. I rewarded him once he went back to a sit. He did very well on this one.

Hide was cotton balls placed inside a desk drawer in the hallway. I detailed a section of lockers as I worked down the hallway towards the desk. Once at the desk Rocky was in odor but was saying the source was coming from the back of the desk. It is possible that is where the odor was leaving the drawer. I opened the drawers slightly allowing him to sniff them more. Once I did this he stayed on the front of the desk right where the source was at. He remained in a sit alert as he waited for his reward.

Worked on Rocky's muzzle fighting again. Started out by having him on leash and having him muzzle hit 2 agitators as they got close to me. He seemed a little confused at first but soon got into it and was hitting them very well. Then moved to picture training in the court hallway. Both agitators sat in the chairs totally still. I gave my commands and sent Rocky in the hallway. He ran down the hallway running right past both agitators in the chairs. He ran up to one, smelling him and then ran off not doing anything. I called him back to me, placing him in a down and giving a command down the hallway again to try and stim him up. I sent him into the hallway again and still he did not engage. It wasn't until one of the agitators starting hitting the side of his chair that he started to engage. Once he did this, I encouraged him to fight. He then started muzzle fighting like he is supposed to. We then moved outside to have an agitator walk away from us, not run simply walk to see what he would do. I gave the command for Rocky to go after him, he took off after him but then slowed down and looked around to see if there was someone else or not before engaging the suspect. I believe he may be getting fixated on equipment and if they do not present a threat to him, he doesn’t want to fight them. Will see about getting a half muzzle to do more muzzle work with him.
worked on up downs and heeling off leash. Bizi also starts off rough while were home but ends well.

worked on bizis recall with tone on is collar. In the morning when we worked on this he didn’t do well wouldn't listen and would not recall to the tone only to my voice. I charged the collar and the remote and in the afternoon he did much better listen to the tone and recall with the remote only.
during tactical advance bizi went after another deputy and I called him off and he recalled and came to my side without going near the deputy.

while doing a building search a suspect came out and I ordered him to get on the ground and he ran. I sent Bizi on an apprahension and he hit the suspect knocking him down. He hit the suspect few more times and them moved away from him when he thought he was no longer a threat. The suspect got up and bizi reengaged and fought the suspect. I did a three phase out and bizi complied perfectly and I had the suspect move away.

suspect hide in a room and we brought bizi into the building and started a building search. When the suspect strted to yell I issued commands and then sent bizi into apprehend. Bizi started to search and was going from room to troom before he identified the right room wnt in and apprehended the suspect.
tactical obedience. I worked further with long line work. Bizi gets inpatient and runs circles around me I worked on him staying on my right side but he was not doing well.
suicidal subject. Had bizi follow a track east and west looking for the subject. Bizi took us to a camper where to juv males were. We were unable to locate the suicidal subject.

after a deputy had already located some controlled substance. I brought bizi to the front passenger light gave bizi the command to search and he yank down the passenger side came to the passenger door and sat at the door. Inside the vehicle on the passenger side was the bag that the controlled substance was.

During active shooter training. Also did some training with Rocky in muzzle. Entered with him in the school as I moved down the hallway clearing it with Deputy Lundberg. Agitator came running out of room and did not do as told and began to run off. I sent Rocky in for the fight. Rocky took off and began fighting him. Later in the day, gave rocky a bite on the bite sleeve as agitator walked off and hid next to a door. I then moved up the hallway, clearing the doorways with Deputy Kelly before getting to Lundberg. He did very well in these drills.

brought bizi to the front passenger light of the vehicle. I gave him the command to search and we made a pass around the vehicle for free air. I then started a systimatic search of the vehicle. On the first pass bizi slowed by the driver's door but keep moving. I got to the passenger door and bizi put his nose to the crack of the door and sat. I kept moving and bizi stayed on the crack then broke and came to me I continued around the vehicle and came to the driver's door where bizi tilted his head up sniff the window then started scratching the driver door and came to a sit. I moved away from bizi and he stayed with the indication on the driver door. He broke for a second went around the front of the vehicle then came back and sat in the same stop then started scratching the door again then sitting again indicationg he was in the odor of narcotics. Meth para was located in the vehicle.

brougt bizi out to assit the city in a drug search. I brought bizi past the drivers door and up to the frontof the vehicle and he pulled me to the passneger side door. As soon as I got to the passenger door the passenger stated he had a marijuana pipe by his seat. Bizi scratched the door and sat outside the passenger door without being given a command. I praised bizi and put him away the pipe and source were confinscated by the city police.

RESPONDED TO STALLINGS TO RUN ROCKY AROUND A VEHICLE THAT HAD BEEN TOWED AFTER AN ARREST HAD BEEN MADE. I EXPLAINED TO J11, BECAUSE THEY HAD ALREADY TOWED THE VEHICLE AND IT WAS SITTING IN AN IMPOUND, IF ROCKY DID ALERT ON THE VEHICLE, IT WOULD NOT GIVE THEM ENOUGH TO ENTER IT FOR A SERCH, I TOLD THEM IF HE ALERTS, THEY WILL BE ABLE TO USE THAT ON POSSIBLY GETTING A WARRANT TO SEARCH THE VEHICLE. I WAS NOT GOING TO RUN ROCKY AROUND IT IF THEY WERE SIMPLY WANTING TO ENTER IT WITHOUT A WARRANT BECAUSE IT HAD BEEN MOVED. THEY STATED THEY AGREED TO THAT. I RAN HIM AROUND THE VEHICLE TWICE, THERE WAS NOT INDICATION OR ALERT, NOT ANY INTEREST IN THE VEHICLE AT ALL.

REFERENCE INCIDENT # 2022-04712 OF A STOLEN VEHICLE RECOVERY, LOCATED A SYRINGE IN THE BACK BED OF THE PICKUP IN A BAG. I THEN RAN ROCKY AROUND THE OUTSIDE OF THE VEHICLE STARTING AT THE FRONT DRIVER SIDE. AS HE WORKED HIS WAY DOWN THE VEHICLE, HE HAD A HEAD JERK AND BEGAN TO BRACKET ON THE DRIVER DOOR, HE CONTINUED DOWN TO THE BACK DRIVER SIDE DOOR WHERE HE WENT TO A FULL SIT ALERT. I WAS NOT ABLE TO PULL HIM AWAY FROM THE DOOR. SEARCHED THE INSIDE OF THE VEHICLE AND DID NOT LOCATE ANYTHING OTHER THEN ANOTHER SYRINGE ON THE BACK FLOOR BOARD ON THE PASSENGER SIDE THAT LOOKED LIKE IT HAD BEEN USED. WAS LATER ADVISED BY FEMALE SUSPECT, THEY DID HAVE METH INSIDE OF THE VEHICLE EARLIER. ROCKY WAS CORRECT IN HIS ALERT.

While at the gun range for firearms training, I took the time to take Rocky out to be around the gun fire. As other people were shooting I stood behind them around 20 yards away. He did great staying at my side or doing what he was told during the live fire. I then walked up getting closer to them and was within 15 feet of them while they were shooting, still did not have any issues. I then moved up to the 7 yard line to shoot with him at my side. I would fire one round at a time. Rocky appeared to be somewhat bothered by this and would jump up from the down position and want to move. Possibly too loud for him. He continued to do this each time with me having to place him in a down with a correction each time. I then had another person stand on his leash holding him in that down while I fired a couple more rounds. He still tried moving from it trying to get closer to me. I then fired several rounds while walking and having him walk with me at my side. This did not appear to bother him at all. He as okay with me shooting as long as we were moving and he was not in the down.
took Bizi for a walk and tried down in motion with a ball at the park. Bizi was so excited to play that the session didn’t go well. I ended the session after trying several times.

brought bizi out while everyone was firing their firearms. He did very well stayed in a down while the gun fire was going off. I then had him heel moved forward and fired my firarm with him at my side he stayed calm and did well.
used treats to do up downs and then made biz stay utside a door in a down for 20 mins. Bizi broke at the very bigining but I placed him back further from the door and he stayed for the whole time.
did some basic obedience around the house while I was sick. Made bizi stay heeled while I cleaned up and he did well.
I placed bizi in the patrol vehicle and left the door open but told him to stay. Bizi did well stayed inn the vehicle until told to get out.

I retrieved Bizi from my patrol vehicle and brought him up towards Kyle's vehicle, walking him past the driver's door. I went to the front of the vehicle, laid him down at the front passenger light, and then gave him the command to search. We made a pass around the vehicle. On the second pass, I started a systematic search in an up-down pattern. I came to the driver's door, and Bizi yanked back, going towards the front of the vehicle, and I released his leash, allowing him to search on his own. I stepped back towards the back side of the vehicle, and Bizi walked down the driver's side door and came to me at the back of the vehicle. I started around the passenger side when Bizi turned back, went to the back driver side bumper, and quickly sat on the corner. He then tried to crawl under the vehicle at that corner and backed out. Then went to the driver's side to the rear driver's side door, sat on the door, and stayed, indicating he was in the odor of narcotics. I walked away around the passenger side Bizi stayed on that door until I retrieved him and returned him to my patrol vehicle. Meth was located in the vehicle.

did open field sends with the intentions of doing a down in motion. On the first send bizi ran stright to the bite ignoring the command. While he was on the bite I tried a 3 phase out and he still ignored the command. I choked bizi off and had the agitator go out of sight. On the second send bizi ignored the command to recall and went to the bite once again. I tried a 3 phase out and he obayed all commands without reengaging. I ended the session on that note.

training.Location: Army National Guard Armory Idaho Falls
training.Notes: Hide was placed under a pallet in the first room. I brought Rocky into the room and placed him in a down as I began to do a pre-walk around the room. I could tell he was in odor already as he was bracketing the air and kept belly crawling away from the spot I placed him in a down. When I got back to him, I gave him the command to search and he began to run around the room running towards the pallet. He sniffed the pallet on one side then began working his way around to the other side of it. Once on the other side he went to a down and stare. I called under the pallet and was told this was correct. I rewarded him on this.

training.Location: Army National Guard Armory Idaho Falls
training.Notes: This hide was placed inside the firewall on the driver side door of one of the vehicles on the property. As I started working Rocky down the vehicle starting at the front driver side head-light, once I got to the driver side door, he began to bracket around the door more then taking a big sniff going to a sit and stare. I called the door and was told this was correct. I rewarded him.

training.Location: Army National Guard Armory Idaho Falls
training.Notes: Hide was placed inside of the bathroom in locker #28. I took Rocky into the bathroom and gave him the command to start his search. I began to detail around the room and then the lockers. Once we got near #28, he began to search more intense on his own. I let him go and he worked his way to #28 going to a sit and stare on this locker. I took the risk and called this locker. I was told this was correct. I rewarded him.

training.Location: Army National Guard Armory Idaho Falls
training.Notes: Hide was behind the passenger seat of another vehicle on the property. I started working Rocky around the front of the vehicle, starting on the front driver side head-light. As I began working my around to the back passenger side and then up towards the front of the vehicle. Rocky was able to jump up and get his nose almost right on the hide itself from behind the canvas of the vehicle. He then went to a very slow sit, jumping back up and staring for a few seconds then going back to a sit and looking up to that area. I called it. This was the hide. I rewarded him.

training.Location: Army National Guard Armory Idaho Falls
training.Notes: Several packages were placed inside the large bay area. I ran Rocky down them presenting down one side then working my way around to the other side. On the first pass down, I noticed a large head jerk on one package and he spent a couple extra seconds on it longer then he did the others before. As we came back along the other side, I noticed he did the same thing. He was also breathing through his mouth more. I made a final pass but this time pressing on each box as I went, burping it. When we got to the box he showed interest in, this time he stuck with it going to a sit on it. I called the box and was told this was correct. I rewarded him on this one.

training.Location: Army National Guard Armory Idaho Falls
training.Notes: The hide was placed on the outside of the bed of a vehicle on the driver side. I began by starting at the front driver side head-light detailing down the side of the vehicle. As Rocky was in odor, he tried going up under the wheel well of the driver side. But did not alert. I continued to present down the side of the vehicle. I noticed he seemed to be bracketing more as we went and then finally hit the hide and went to a sit right away. I called it and was told this was correct.

training.Location: Army National Guard Armory Idaho Falls
training.Notes: The hide was in the weight room, sitting under a 45lb plate. I began by detailing around the room, detailing a couple machines as we moved around the room, the weight was sitting near a machine on the floor. I presented the weight and began to move as Rocky checked it. He did not move with me and stayed on the weight going to a down and stare at it. I called the weight as the source and was told this was correct.

training.Location: Army National Guard Armory Idaho Falls
training.Notes: Hide was an open area search and was placed under the pallet that a generator was sitting on. I walked Rocky into the area and gave him the command to search. Rocky was in odor right away but could ot figure out where it was coming from. He kept working around the generator but would not go under it far enough at first. Then he finally checked under getting closer to the source and went to a down and stare. I called under the pallet where he was at and told I was within range it was correct. I rewarded him.

ASSISTED ISP WITH SEARCH OF A VEHICLE WITH ROCKY. I HEARD THEM ASK FOR A K9 FROM BONNEVILLE BUT BCSO DID NOT HAVE ONE THAT COULD RESPOND. I MADE CONTACT WITH TROOPER COX WHO WAS ON THE TRAFFIC STOP AND EXPLAINED TO HIM I COULD RESPOND WITH ROCKY. UPON ARRIVING I BEGAN BY RUNNING ROCKY AROUND THE OUTSIDE OF THE VEHICLE DOING A FREE AIR SNIFF. ROCKY ALERTED ON THE DRIVER SIDE DOOR AND BACK REAR PASSENGER SIDE OF THE VEHICLE. DURING THE SEARCH OF THE VEHICLE, ISP LOCATED METHAMPHETAMINE INSIDE O THE VEHICLE. I REURNED TO THE AREA THE ITEMS WERE LOCATED WITH ROCKY, ONCE HE ALERTED ON IT AGAIN, I REWARDED HIM AND PRAISED HIM UP BEFORE RETURNING HIM TO THE VEHICLE AND CLEARING THE AREA.

Started off by sending Rocky on a straight bite and then attempting a "3 phase out" off the bite. He did very well coming off the bite but as soon as the agitator started to move away, he tried to re-engage him again. I used the e-collar to correct him to place him back in a down. While correcting him with the e-collar, he ran back to me, but as soon as he laid down in front of me the correction stopped. I then sent him for a bite again. This time on the "3 phase out" he came off it and stayed down and did not try to re-enage. I walked up to him, hooked him up to my leash and dismissed the agitator. I prasied him up and took him back. We did this one more time and he did very well coming off the bite again and staying down. I praised him up a lot and then took him back.

After working on his "3 phase out" we started to work on his down in motion. I sent him in for a bite, as he got within 30 yards of the agitator, I gave him the command to go to a down. He was not going down right away so I did use the e-collar to correct him. It took a little tap of the e-collar and he went down to the ground. I approached him and was able to hook him up. I made a second attempt with the down in motion, this time sending him to the bite, once he got to the same area, I gave the command to go down and he went to a down right away. No correction was needed. I was able to walk up to him and hook him up. I dismissed the agitator and prasied Rocky a lot while taking him back to vehicle to put him up and allow him to rest. Ended on a good note.

Checked his handler protection and call off from the bite. He did not have any issues doing a handler protection and once he was on the bite, I stepped away and started a "3 phase out" he came off the bite going to a down and staying there until I was able to hook him up. I praised him up and placed him back in the vehicle, ending on this high note again.

training.Location: Idaho Falls City PD Training Building
training.Notes: This was bark drills both inside and outside. Started by going inside. I did not know where agitator was, but he was hiding behind a door inside of the building somewhere. I placed Rocky in a down in the doorway and issued my commands into the building. I sent Rocky in to search. I waited for Rocky as he hunted through the building. Rocky ended up running upstairs and began barking at a door. I called the door and was told this was correct the agitator was behind that door. After the agitator got to stim him up some, I took him outside where he did an open area bark drill. I issued my commands and sent Rocky into the search area I was told. As Rocky was running pass a utility trailer, I noticed the head snap back to the area of the trailer telling me he had caught odor of someone. Rocky went to the trailer and began sniffing around it. He got to the back of it near the main doors of it and sat and began barking at the trailer. I called this and was told the agitator was inside. I allowed the agitator to stim Rocky up as his reward before praising him up and placing him back in the vehicle.

Took Rocky out into the crowd at the Mud Lake Rodeo at the fair grounds. I had him in muzzle and walked him around the area trying to keep him at my side. He did try and pull away from me at first but then stuck at my side more as we kept walking around. He also did very well with people walking around him and was not trying to muzzle check them like he normally would. After some time of this, I walked him back to my vehicle where I praised him and placed him back in my vehicle.

Worked on his down and stay. Would place him in a down and keep him there for 5 minutes at a time making sure he did not break the down. I did this 3 different times. He stayed in the down each time for the full 5 minutes.

Tested his "3 phase out" again. Just to make sure he is still doing what he is supposed to do. Gave the command for agitator to come out and then sent Rocky on the bite. Once he was on the bite I let him fight for a few minutes and then I gave the command to start getting him off the bite. He came off the bite without any issues. I told the agitator to slowly step away and Rocky stayed in place. I was able to approach Rocky and hook him back up without him trying to re-engage again. Agitator was dismissed and I praised Rocky and put him up. He did very well.

This was an open area search. Hide was placed inside of a tote that was outside and then the lid placed back on top of it. I parked on the other side of the parking lot as far away from the hide as possible. I allowed Rocky to run around on his own. When he started to run over into that area, I noticed a head jerk back towards the tote and then he began to go towards it. As I walked over, I could see he was working around the tote sniffing it. He then went to a sit and stare on his own. No command to search was given but he picked up the odor on his own and located the hide.

Searched 3 vehicles in the back part of the fire station. The vehicles are vehicles the fire department uses to practices taking apart so there is a lot of broken glass and jagged edges around them. The first vehicle, (white in color) was a blank vehicle. I ran Rocky around it and he did not alert or show any interest in it at all. I then went to the second vehicle (green in color) and began to run Rocky around it. Once he got to the driver side door, he began to braket around it and then jumped up towards the window some. I stopped him from jumping inside the vehicle keeping him on the outside of it for his safety. He then went to an alert on the door. The hide was inside the fire wall of the door.

This hide was inside the third vehicle (marron in color) in the front driver side under the hood. As I was approaching the vehicle with Rocky, he ran straight to the area the hide was in and sniffed the hood area and then went to a sit. The wind was blowing directly towrds us as we were approaching the vehicle so I believe he was in odor the entire time. I rewarded him on this.

Hide was placed under the counter in the break room near the coffee machine. I began by detailing around the room. Rocky was moving very fast, so I had to spin him around a couple time to make sure he sniffed several areas before moving on. It is possible he was in odor and was trying to get to it but I wanted to detail the room so he keeps that mentality with me. Once we got to the area the hide was at, He went past it at first but then went back to it. I tried to pull him away from it but he would not move. He was frozen in place and the more I tried to pull him away, the harder he stuck with it. I then rewarded him for this.

Hide was in the bottom locker in the mens bathroom. When we entered the bathroom, Rocky started to bracket right away and began to sniff down the wall from the door going straight back to the lockers. Once there, he went to the corner of the room and then began working his way back down them. Once he got to locker #14 where the hide was located, he went to a sit and stare. I rewarded him

HAD A DEPUTY HIDE A SMALL COTTON BALL ON A VEHCLE AT THE SHERIFFS OFFICE. I BROUGHT BIZI TO THE AREA AND LAID HIM DOWN. I ISSUED THE COMMAND TO SEARCH AND WE WENT A PASS AROUND AND ON THE PASSENGERSIDE NEAR THE BACK DOOR I SAW BIZI DOUBLE TAKE BUT CONTINUE. WE REACHED THE FRONT OF THE VEHICLE AND HE TURNED ON HIS OWN I LET GO OF MY LEASH AND LET HIM GO BACK DOWN THE PASSENGER SIDE WHERE HE CAME TO THE REAR PASSENGER DOOR AND THEN LAID DOWN AND STARTED CRAWLING UNDER THE VEHICLE. BII STOPPED AND JUST STARED AT THE DOOR AT THE BOTTOM OF THE DOOR. SOURCE WAS HIDDEN ON THE FLOOR BOARD IN THE BACK SEAT.

had deputies hide small cotton balls on a old vehicle behind the fire station. The source was hidden in the center console. I brought bizi to the front of the vehicle to the passenger light. I laid him down and walked around I gave him the command to search and we got to the driver door and bizi s head went high in the area and he slowed smelling the door. I kept moving and he followed after me. We went arounf the rear of the vehicle and and bizi pulled me back around to the driver door. He again stayed by the door but didn’t indicate I gave the command to search and he pulled me around the front of the vehicle and pulled to the passenger side of the vehicle came to front passenger door sat and started scratching the door before laying down. Temp was 92 and the wind was blowing from the south trhough the vehicle.

first sent bizi on a open field apprehension. I issued commands and he did well staying in a down. I released him and he went in for the apprehension. I noticed he bit high then moved to a leg lower. I did a three phase out and he followed commands perfectly without reengaging.

I brought bizi back to the start point after the first bite and asked the trainer to do another open field stright send. I gave commands softly and sent bizi on the apprehension. Bizi hit low and stayed on the bite but as soon as I came close to do a three phase out he released and bit the other leg. I called the three phase out and he did well and while the agitator was walking away he rengaged. I corrected him with the ecollar and reissued commands on the three phase out. He did well and followed commands.
worked on tie backs with bizi to make sure he wasn’t releasing on his bites. During this drill bizi did very well didn’t try to re bite of change bite areas.

got bizi inn position to do open field apprehension and down in motion. I gave commands and sent bizi on the apprehension as he ran in I gave the command to recall. When I saw that Bizi wasn’t listening I quickly gave the command to lay down and he obeyed. I then recalled Bizi to me and he came right back and heeled to my side. I praised him up and put him away.

had a suspect hide in the upstairs of a traing facitlity behind a closed door. I brought Bizi to the doorway gave commands and sent bizi in. I allowed Bizi to search the building on his own. Bizi searched the downstaries first and when he passed a hallway he flipped around and came back to the hallway and went out of my sight. I could hear that he was still searching and allowed him to continue. After approximately 3 minutes bizi started barking and scratching a door. I went to find him and he was infront of the door where the suspect was hiding. The susect opened the door and played peek a boo with him and I took him away.

suspect was hidden in a trailer in a large field. I gave commands and released bizi. Bizi ran in the oppisate direction of the search area and I had to recall him and try and get him in the right area. After about 2 minutes f that I finally got bizi going in the right direction and I saw his head flip and he started running in front of a truck and the trailer the suspect was in. Bizi narrowed it down an went circles around the trailer looking for a way in. when he couldn’t get in he tried crawling under the vehicle to get in. Bizi finally came to the rear of the traielr and started to scratch and bark indicating he had found something.

laid a half mile track through the woods. I brought bizi to the start and laid him down walked about 15 feet ahead of him then returned to him I gave him the command to search and he started running faster than I could keep up so I released the line and ran behind following. We hit a hard corner I had done and he ran right over it. I let him keep going and he relized he had lost the scent and turned around and slowly moved back to where the corner was. Bizi got the track and then started moving fast again. I picked up the line and was ale to keep up as he had slowed down. Bizi stayed on track until we got to the toy I had placed.

laid another half mile track and laid Bizi down wlaked into the area about 15 feet and returned to bizi. I gave the command to search and he took off running in the direction of the track we went about 100 yards and bizi turned away from the track and we went about 100 yards before he came back to me and was just sniffing around. I took him back to where he lost the track and restarted. We got about halfway when he lost the tack again and this time I just stood and let him find it on his own. Once he found it we went alll the way to the end and he found the toy on his own.

laid a mile long track. I brought bizi to the start of the track walked 15 feet in and returned and gave command to search. Everything was going good until we hit a hard corner I had laid and he went over it and kept going the wrong way. When he losted it I let him try and find it on his own and he took me even further away from the track. We never were able to pick the track back up and I took him back to the house.

I brought Bizi up past Justin's vehicle to the front of it and then turned him around without giving any commands and started walking back past the driver's door. We walked past the driver's door around the backside of the vehicle, and we were getting ready to walk up the passenger side when Bizi flipped around, pulled me back to the rear of the vehicle, and sat on the rear driver's side. Bizi then started to scratch the vehicle, indicating that he was in the odor of narcotics. I released Bizi's leash and stepped away from him. He stayed on the vehicle in a sit position until he became frustrated and started to scratch the vehicle, indicating that he was in the order of narcotics. I took Bizi away and returned him to my vehicle. Controlled substances were found after searching.

hide source on a jc vehicle in the parking lot. I brought bizi to the front passenger light and laid him down. Bizi immediately lifted his head and started to crawl. I was walking arounf the vehicle when I came around he was crawling down the side of the vehicle. I gave him the command to search and he ran to the crack between the cab and the bed of the truck. Biz went on his hind legs and then sat and quickly started scracthing before going to another sit indication. The deputy who placed the source stated he was right on it.
I did tie back drills to ensure bizi was staying on the bite and not releaseing to go to another spot. Bizi did well over three drills never releasing to go to another spot.

Brought bizi to the start of an open field apprehension. I sent bizi on the bite after giving commands and he bite high but moved to a leg. I came in and started a three phase out and Bizi listen to all commands and didn’t reengage.
Brought bizi back to the beginning and reissued commands I sent bizion the bite and he did well staying on the bite without rebiting. I issued 3 phase out commands and he did good not reengaing.

brought bizi to the start of the open field send and issued warnings. I sent him on the bite and called out for a down in motion and he went down on command. I gave the command to bite and he went in and bit. I did a three phase out and he listen to commands perfectly so I ended it and put him away.
walked bizi around a blank vehicle giving him the command to search and he walked around the vehicle and then did a systematic search bizi never indicated.

Hide was placed inside the front bumper on the outside of the vehicle. I started by working him around the front of the vehicle near the driver side and going around. Rocky first tried to alert on the back driver side panel but as I continued around, he did not stay and followed me. As I got back to the front bumper on the passenger side, he sniffed much harder and went to a sit alert a lot faster and would not move away from it. I called this and was told this was correct. I rewarded him.

Hide was placed in the bathroom, behind the water shut off panel. The first time I ran him through the bathroom, he did not alert on the hide but I did not present it and he was tired from searching the other rooms and vehicles. The time he alerted was the second time I took him into the bathroom in an attempt to see if there was anything there. This time I did present the panel and once I did he alerted to it and stayed. I called this and was told this was correct. I rewarded him.

This hide was placed between the right rear tires on vehicle #2. Rocky did not alert on this hide until the second time I attempted to locate it. He at first was showing a lot of interest on the other side of the vehicle. It is possible the odor was traveling through to that side. I did not call anything at that time but waited. On this second attempt, he located it between the tires and actually pulled it out himself. I called it (as he pulled it out) and rewarded him

Hide was placed in the bottom of the cabinet in room #4. As we entered the room, I gave Rocky the command to search and was allowing hima free run on his own at first. He went straight to the cabinet and sent to a sit, He would not leave it and started to bite the bottom of cabinet. I called this and was told this was correct. I rewarded him

Hide was placed inside the binocular case on the inside of the vehicle sitting on the floorboard of the vehicle. Once I placed Rocky on the inside of the vehicle, he began to search the inside of the vehicle. Once he located the case, he sniffed it and then started to bite at it. I called this as the source. I was told this was correct. I rewarded him.

Hide was placed in the bottom drawer of the stove inside of the kitchen. Rocky first showed a lot of interest in the upper level of the stove. I was unsure where he was trying to alert to so I presented the area several times. I eventually presented the bottom of the stove where he started to bite at it more. I called this and was told it was correct. I rewarded him

Unsure how many grams, but hide was placed in a box in the lobby of the fire station. I presented all the boxes to him and he stuck with one and did not leave it. I called the box and was told this was correct. I rewarded him

Hide was placed outside along the fence. Unsure how many grams it was. I started but running Rocky out towards the fence line. As I moved to start a grid pattern, he did not come with me and started going down the fence himself. I allowed him to go searching the area on his own. He got the source of the hide and ended up digging it up and pulling it out. As He did and I seen this, I called this and rewarded him.

Bark drill inside the fire station. Agitator was hidden inside of the closet in the training room. Placed Rocky in a down in the hallway and issued warnings and then sent him in on a search. He hunted through the area well checking the rooms he could get into as he went. I noticed he kept sniffing high telling me he was getting odor from the ceiling but was able to work it to the door of the closet where he began to bark and alert. I called this.

Checked all of his obedience in the field. Started with a 5 minute down and stay. I placed him in a down and left him there for the 5 minutes. He stayed as he was supposed to. Later checked his on leash and off leash heeling, was told I passed but I do need to work on this more with him still, once he is off leash, he feels like he can do what he wants and tries to run off some. Then had him jump over a concrete barrier and placed him in a down on the other side of it. He did well with it. Then while using a starter pistol. I fired 2 rounds with him next to me. He stayed next to me and did not try and run off.

Had to test his bite work. First started by sending him on the bite and then giving him the command to go to a down in motion. At first he ran through going straight to the bite. I corrected him, and after a few minutes of making sure he listened, I attempted it a second time. This time he went to a down and stayed until I was able to pick him up. I then sent him on a straight bite allowing him to bite and then calling him off using a (3 phase out) he came right off without any issues. I was able to walk up to him and pick him up without issues. Then during the handler protection, he did engage the the agitator and then during the fight, I was able to call him off again using the 3 phase out.

This was an open area bark drill. I placed him in a down and issued warnings, then sent him out to look for the agitator. As he was searching, I noticed a head jerk as he got towards the building the agitator was in. He wento to the building sniffing it and then started barking on it. I called this.

Hide was placed on the outside of rear bumper of the vehicle. As I was walking Rocky into the bay area and was being told what vehicles were par to of the search, Rocky hit odor and went to an alert right away. I was unable to move him and get him to come with me so I called this as the hide and was told this was correct. I rewarded him on this.

Hide was placed inside the bathroom in the toilet paper holder. As Rocky and I entered the room, he hit the paper holder and went to an alert. I called this as the hide and was told this was correct. I rewarded him.

Hide was placed on the outside of the vehicle inside the battery box on the driver side. As I ran Rocky around the vehicle I started on the front passenger side working towards the rear of the vehicle. As I came around to the driver side and got to the area the hide was in, Rocky began to bracket more around that are and eventually sticking to the box. He sat and started directly at the box. I called this as the source of the hide and was told this was correct. I rewarded him.

Hide was in the bottom drawer on the last sleeping area upstairs. As I entered the area and began my search, Rocky went straight to the drawer and sniffed it and then went to a down and stayed there staring at the drawer. I called this and was told this was correct.

Hide was placed inside the center console near the radio of the vehicle. I ran Rocky around the outside of the vehicle first and he alerted on the outside of the vehicle on the back driver side door. I placed him inside the vehicle to let him search the inside of it. He hit the source of the hide and went to a stare directly at it. I called this the source of the hide and was told it was correct. I rewarded him.

Hide was placed under the bed inside the bed frame in another sleeping area. I presented around the room and Rocky first alerted to the power outlet approx 2 feet away from the source. I was told to pin-point the source as I was within 3 feet of it but that was not the area the hide wa in. I detailed the area again and he began to sniff under the bed and then went to a down and stare. I called under the bed on the corner of it. I was told this was correct. I rewarded him.

Hide was inside the 4th box in a row of 5 boxes. I began by placing him in a down and walking down the line, "burping" each box. Once I was done, I gave him the command to search and we began searching the boxes, one our first pass by, I noticed the head jerk on the box but he did not stay, so when we turned around and started to come back, he hit it again but stayed with it this time. I called this as the source and was told this was correct. I rewarded him on this.

Hide was placed outside under some pallets. I took Rocky off leash and gave him the command to search and just let him run the area on his own to see if he could locate the hide. He was able to pick up the odor and locate the hide. I rewarded him once he did.

source was hidden in the front bumper of a vehicle. Near the entrance of the search area. I brought bizi in and he pulled to the front of the vehicle I let him go because he was showing his signs that he was in odor. Bizi moved around the vehicle to the passenger door but quickly turned around came in front of the vehicle and laid down staring at the bumper then got up pawed at it and quickly sat again.

source was hidden behind the water shut off in the bathroom. I brought bizi to the entrance of the bathroom. Due to the small space I gave bizi the command to search and allowed him to search off lead. Bizi moved around the area and went to the far wall then moved to the west wall and moved up and down it moving back towards the entrance. I could see that he was in odor as he was sniffing hard and had his mouth closed. He came to a small box and put his nose on it and sniffed hard then started to scratch at it. He scratched at it several times then sat and stared. The source was hidden inside of it.

source was hidden in between the back tires on a vehicle. I brought bizi to a vehicle I was told to search and I started the search around it. This vehicle was park directly next to the source vehicle. The vehicle I was search was a blank vehicle. While bizi and I were coming down the driver side of the blank vehicle I saw his mouth close tight and his head flipped back but he kept moving with me. We rounded the backside of the vehicle and bizi then pulled me back to the drivers side. I followed and he went to the source vehicle and went to the back tires. Bizi crawled up under the vehicle and was laying in front of the back tires he started to scratch and bite at the tire. I looked to the grader and told him id call it and then Bizi pulled the source out from the tires.

source was hidden in a bottom drawer in a small office. I brought bizi to the entrance took him off leash and gave him the command to search. Bizi blasted into the room moving very quick. I called him to me slowed him down and started to present a cabinet that was close to the entrance. Bizi put his nose to the bottom of the cabinet and laid down with his nose on the bottom drawer. I called the hide and he then started to scratch the drawer and bark indicating that he was in odor.

source was hidden inside a vehicle inside a binocular case in the center of the vehicle. I brought bizi to the front passenger light of the vehicle and laid him down. I could see that he was already in odor as he was tilting his head back and was crawling towards the vehicle sniffing with his mouth closed. I walked around the vehicle to check for obstacles. I gave bizi the command to search and we went around the front to the drivers door and he got on his hind legs and sniffed the crack of the door hard and then we kept moving. We went around the back and to the passenger door and he did the same thing but then sat and stared and then scrathed the door. I put bizi inside the vehicle and he went to the center and with his hind legs on the seat and front paws on the floor he sat and stared at the case.

source was hidden in the kitchen inside the stove bottom drawer. I brought bizi to the entrance walked the room for obstacles and got bizi and gave the command to search. I let bizi free air sniff the room then brought him back to the start and strated a systematic search. As we moved throught the room in a up and down manner I had bizi check the top of the stove then the bottom and when he went to the bottom of the stove and he laid down and put his nose on the stove and quickly started to scratch indicating he was in odor.

source was place in a box of 6 spread out throughout the room. I brought bizi into the room and he pulled away from be and went to a box near a cabinet and started scratching and biting it. I quickly grabbed bizi so he didn’t destroy the box or source. I called the hide and it was a positive indication. Bizi found this without been given the command.

source was hidden on a fence line in a large area search. I brought bizi to the area and stated him on a grid search of the area. I started on the south side and moved north. About halfway through the large area bizi broke from the grid search and went to the fence line on the north part of the area. Bizi moved down the fence line and came to a small metal plate and started to scratch at it and then stood and stared and then scratched again. The source was hidden under the plate.

brought bizi to a blank room and took him off leash to search the small office. Bizi moved around the office and I did a systematic search with him. I didn’t see any pre indicators that he was in odor but he went to a large cabinet got o his hind legs and then scratched the bottom drawer and sat. I called the bottom drawer and the grader informed me there was nothing hidden in the room.

deputy stopped a vehicle leaving a known drug house after been given a tip that he was going to buy drugs there. The suspect was taken from the vehicle and sat on the back driver side bumper of his vehicle. Shortly after being sat on the bumper he was given the sfsts. I ran bizi around the vehicle on a free air sniff and he indicated on the back bumer where the suspect was sitting. I informed the deputy and the suspect was searched. Nothing was found on the suspect and I conducted a pc search of the vehicle. I was not able to find anything in the truck so I brought biz to see if he could pinpoint. I put bizi in the vehicle and he immediately sat on the drivers seat then started to scratch it and stare at it. I tried to pull bizi out of the vehicle and he wouldn’t move from the indication. I got biz out and search all around the drivers seat and couldn’t find a source. Shortly after the suspect stated he wanted tot speak with detectives about drugs being sold at the residence that he had just left.

suspect ran from a physical disturbance and bizi and I were brought in to track and find the suspect. When we arrived a deputy located and took the suspect into custody. We were unsure if there was another suspect so I deployed bizi to search the area. After a long search bizi was not able to find anyone else in the area.

WAS CONTACTED BY 233 TO POSSIBY SEARCH A VEHICLE WITH ROCKY. LOOKING INSIDE OF THE VEHICLE, I COULD SEE WHAT APPEARED TO BE 10-15 AIR FRESHNERS INSIDE OF IT.  IN MY TRAINING, THIS INDICATES THEY ARE TRYING TO HIDE THE SMELL OF SOMETHING ELSE. THERE WAS ALSO A LARGE MARIJUANA PLANT GROWING RIGHT NEXT TO THE VEHICLE AND SUSPECTS THAT WERE ARRESTED, HAD BEEN SEEN FLEEING FROM THE VEHICLE. I RAN ROCKY AROUND THE VEHICLE AND HE ALERTED ON THE PASSENGER SIDE DOOR, AWAY FROM THE PLANT GROWING. UPON CONDUCTING A SEARCH OF THE VEHICLE, MARIJUANA RESIDUE HAD BEEN LOCATED INSIDE OF IT. I BROUGHT ROCKY BACK AND WHEN HE ALERTED ON THE VEHICLE, I REWARDED HIM FOR THIS
heeling on leash with several turns. Bizi heels very well no issues.
heeling off leash with several turns. Bizi does very well with this.

sent bizi on a apprehension aggitator came and I gave the command and released him about 30 feet halfway between me and the aggitator I gave the command to down. Bizi ran through the command and went to the aggitator. I called him off and recalled him. Bizi complied and I brought him back to the start. I had the agitator hide and reemerge I gave the command to apprehend and then the command to down. Bizi complied and then I recalled him to my side. On the second round bizi complied with all commands.
placed bizi in a down and walked about 30 feet away and stood and spoke with others in a group. Bizi maintained his down for 5 minutes with no issues.

ran bizi up to a cement barrier and had him jump over as soon as he did I gave the command to down and he complied I then recalled him and he jumped back over the barrier and I down him again. Bizi complied and I called him to a heel.
while havng bizi hel to my side I fired 2 shots and he didn’t move away or jump.

brought bizi to the beginning of the search and issued commands. The suspect was hidden in a closet in a large room. I released bizi and he started a search. As he ran into the large room I saw his head tilt up and he started to move back and fourth right inside the doorway. The suspect was hidden in the closet just to the right of the entrance. He moved towards the door and out of my sight. I could hear him sniffing and scratching at the door then he let out several barks indicating he had found something he couldn’t get too. I came to him and he was sitting infront of the closet door where the suspect was hiding.

suspect was hidden in a small building in a large open field. I brought bizi to the edge of the field and issued commands. The suspect was hidden approximatley 100 yards to the west of where I was sending bizi. I released bizi and he ran to the north of the small building and I saw his head flip towards the building and he ran to the door of the building. He sniffed along the door and then ran around it a few times then came back to the door scratched he sat infront of it for  few seconds then let out several barks indicating he had found something he couldn’t get too.

while walking through the park had a suspect hide and as I walked past the suspect attaked me. Bizi immediately went to my protection biting the suspect. I issued my 3 commands to release and bizi complied on the first try.

built a sit table at my house and brought bizi to the edge. I only rewarded bizi if he sat immediately. Did this several times until he understood the game. He started sitting as soon as we came to the edge and did well after several trys will keep working this.

sit table at my house and brought bizi to the edge. I only rewarded bizi if he sat immediately. Did this several times. He started sitting as soon as we came to the edge and did well after several trys. When I started he would try and jump up to get toy will keep working this.
still working the sit table to reenforce his sit to receive the toy. Bizi is doing well but still very amped to get the toy.

while at home biz has become increaslingly more intrested in food that others have. Using the collar id correct this behavior when he would try and get food of counters or from plates. It only took one correction and he stopped doing what he was doing. I worked on obedience heeling and sharp turns. We also worked on his up downs and his staying in position for long periods.

door pop drills. Bizi loves this game we worked it a little differen. I'd open the door and if im standing there I make him stay in the vehicle and I walk to the rear of the vehicle and open the back hatch with his door open and make him stay in it. It took a few trys but he got the hang of it. I then moved to door pop drills where I was out f sight. With the drill we had just done he was hesitate to get out but got out and came to find me. He found me each time without a problem. I then moved back to the drill of opening by the door and walking to the rear. He made the switch good and we moved back and fourth and he did well with each switch recongnizing each drill.

through out the day work sit table drills. Bizi has got back in the hang of this and is doing well. Will move onto working on mutliple know hide sit drills to get him back in the hang of it. Getting him to sit indicate on dope versus his scratch and sit indication. Also making him stay with the dope.

brought bizi into the garage where the vehicle that the hide was hidden on was parked. As we walked through the door bizi pulled me the bumper of a vehcile and started to try and get under the vehicle. He then started to scratch the bumper and and then quickly laid down staring at the bumper. I called the hide and the grader stated it was correct.

source was hidden in the bathroom in a toilet paper despenser. I brought bizi to the door and took him off leash to search as the bathroom was small. I gave the command to search and bizi came in and started searching the room. He ran through the room and I could see he was in odor by the toilet but wasn’t sticking with anything and just kept moving around the toilet. I moved to a position to start a systematic search for bizi to search certain areas. I statered presenting things and had biz search them and moved around the room. Bizi moved back on his own with his head in the air to the toilet and was sniffing hard around it. Bizi just kept moving around the area without indicating. I knew he was in odor but just wasn’t fining the source to indicate. I told the grader I wanted tot come back to the room after doing another hide. When we returned I presented the room in the other direction and when we came to the toilet despenser bizi scratched at it and it fell open exposing the source. Bizi sat and then scratched again.

source was hidden in a battery box below the staris of the driver's door. I brought bizi to the front passengerside bumper and then walked around the vehicle checking for hazards. When I returned to bizi I gave him the command to search and we moved quickly around the vehicle free air scenting the vehicle. On the second pass I started a systematic search and moved around the vehicle. As we came to the battery box I presented above it on the door and bizi went up over the source. When he came down I kept moving and he moved with me but quickly flipped his head back and pulled back to the batterybox. I released his leash allowed him to go back and he sniffed on the box with his nose touching it then started to scratch he then sat indicating he was in odor. I moved away from him and he stayed with the dope. I called the hide and the grader indicated it was correct.

source was hidden in a dresser drawer in the bottom drawer. I brought bizi to the small room took him off leash to allow him to search freely and gve him the command he went through the room searching freely when he came to the drawer he passed it but quickly flipped his head went to the bottom drawer and sniffed hard scratch slightly and laid down staring at the drawer. I called the hide and the grader indicated it was correct.

source was hidden inside a vehicle in the center console. I brought bizi to the front passenger headlight and gave him the command to search. We rounded the driver side and as we made our way back to the rear bumper bizi's head flipped and he pulled back to the driver door. When he got to the door he went on his hind legs sniffing through an open window and then sat. I called the hide and the grader stated to pinpoint. I opened the door and bizi jumped in went to the back seat and then put his paws on the center console with his nose on it sniffing hard. Bizi then stopped and stared. I called the hide and the grader stated it was correct.

source was hidden in the bed frame in a small room. I brought bizi to the entrance and laid him down while I was looking in the room I looked back at bizi and his head was tilted back and he started crawling forward towards the bed. I gave the command to search because I could tell he was in odor and he went to the bed and tried to go under it when he realized he couldn't go under he scracthed then laid down by the bed. I called the hide and the grader stated it was correct.

several boxes were laid out, the source was hidden in the 4 box in a line. I brought biz in and laid him down and walk by each box pushing down on them. I gave bizi the command to search and he moved down the line quickly. I brought him back and presented each box. Bizi showed slight intrest on the source box but moved off it going to another deputy that was standing by. I brought bizi back to the boxes and presented again. Bizi showed intrest again but moved away towards the deputies. I told the grader I wanted to move on and left the room. When I came back I presented each box and stayed by each box longer. Ensuring bizi was sniffing properly. When we came to the source box bizi sniffed and lifted his head but then quickly sniffed hard again and put his nose deep into the box. He lifted his head and stood and stared. I called the box and right as I did bizi started to scratch it like crazy exposing the source.

source was hidden outside in a large wood pile. I brought bizi to the area and gave the command to search. We first searched down a fence line. When we got to the end of the fence line I saw bizi flip his head back and he started pulling me to the wood pile I allowed him to go on his own. He came to a small box and started scratching vigorously before stopping and staring at it. I called the hide and the grader indicated it was correct.

searched a blank vehicle and saw no indications from bizi at all. He searched vigorously but no indications were made. Also searched a blank room and no indications were made after going through the room bizi exited on his own going to a room with source.

RAN ROCKY AROUND THE OUTSIDE OF THE VEHICLE THAT WAS LEFT ABONDONDED ON PRIVATE PROPERTY. ROCKY ALERTED ON IT. DURING SEARCH OF THE VEHICLE. WE LOCATED SMALL AMOUNT OF MARIJUANA INSIDE OF THE VEHICLE.

Agitator was hidden in the entry way to the court rooms at far end of hallway. I placed Rocky in a down and issued my commands for suspect to come out. They did not so I sent him. He hunted the area well until he located the agitator and went for the bite. I then did a choke off allowing him to chase the agitator out of the area. Everything went smoothly except the agitators need to know how to agitate and make it seem more real for the dogs.

Did a muzzle fight with Rocky with agitator hiding behind 2, 1-ton straw bails stacked on each other. I issued the warnings after placing Rocky in a down and then sent him. He hunted the area, as the agitator kept moving around to hide from him. Rocky was able to pick up scent from agitator and engaged him. He did very well fighting him even when agitator started to jump on top of bails, Rocky jumped up as well to continue fighting. I hooked him up and we did a chase off with peek a boos to end it.

Laid a track through the field and let it sit for 30 minutes before running him on it. He did well sticking with it at first but then came off it and wanted to pay attention to people walking around the area. I had to direct him to get back on the track. He continued to come off it but would then find it again on his own. He was able to follow track all the way to his toy.

IFPD was doing throws with odors into the grass with thir new dogs. I also did some of the same with Rocky, it doesn’t hurt to go back to basics at times. He did well locating his toy with the various odors in it.
Used the pillow to work his bark alert He did great knowing what to do right away. I then placed the pillow where he couldn’t get it and when he started to bark, I would make it available to him.

Laid a track that went almost straight out through the grain field for a mile. I added a few slight turns to it but kept it straight for the most part to see what he would do. He did well, only zig-zagging back and forth but stuck with it till he located his toy

Worked his on and off leash heel. He still wants to try and run out in front of me some but he does listen well and comes back when told. Not sure why he just doesn’t want to stay at my side, will continue working this

Took Rocky to the High School football field and had him run up and down the bleachers as they are different and they had a game ealier there. I wanted him to get used to the feel of them and the different odors from everyone that was there. He did well and did not try and eat anything even though he did come across several food items left from the game.

Took him to the large grass area near the church and used his toys to work on his "down-in-motion" I threw the balls for him at first allowing him to just run through and get them but then I started to add the command to go to a down. He did well, going to a down and staying with it while waiting for the next toy to be thrown in. I then ended it when he went to a down and waited for me to come pick him up.
Worked on his down and stay. I started him at 5 minutes, then moved to 10, then 15. He did well with it. I would remind him at each 5 minute mark to stay down. He did as told.
Laid a short track through the yard before we did anything else. He did well, again with the zig-zag but stuck with it. Located his toy under the tree.

I noticed the head jerk and him braketing around it but he did not alert until I got him up onto the mower itself and he was able to get his nose right under the seat. He then alerted to it.

Hide was placed inside the bbq grill. I ran him around the jetskis first then spun him and detailed around the grill, at first he didn’t stay with it but did show interest on the front of it. Once I ran him on the back and more open area, he hit the odor more and stuck with it going to an alert.

Hide was cotton balls wih odor on them that were placed inside an altoids can and then stuck under the ac unit outside of the church. At approximately 2:00 PM on October 2, 2022, in the county of Jefferson, I was called out by Deputy McRae and Deputy Hammar for a K9 search for a wanted suspect located at 3879 E. 100 N.

Upon arrival, Deputy Hammar informed me that we had been given consent to search the home, but also exigent circumstances applied. The circumstances were the individuals inside the home giving false information about who he was and had two warrants out of Colorado and one out of Ada county Idaho. The neighbor had called in and told Deputy Hammar that he knew the individual personally and knew that he was inside the home while we were there.

I approached the doorway, laid busy down in the doorway, and issued three commands that a sheriff K9 would be released into the home if he didn't surrender and come out quietly. With no answer, I released Bizi into the home, and he searched vigorously every room. After Bizi had searched, Deputy Hammar and I went in to ensure the home was clear. Discovering that the home was clear, we moved to the backyard to check the outbuilding to see if the individual was hiding there. Bizi searched the outside and the outbuilding and could not find anyone hiding. I noticed on the west side of the outbuilding that on my way back to my squad car, Bizi's mannerism changed, and he went towards the northwest corner of the backyard. I gave Bizi the command to track, and he put his nose to the ground and started moving back and forth throughout the yard, coming to a fence.

When I got to the fence, Bizi showed interest and kept moving back and forth along the fence line. Around this time, Dispatch sent a photo of Joseph O'Neill to my phone. I lifted the fence and let Bizi go under. I climbed over and followed behind Bizi as he was still tracking. We hit an open field, and Bizi started to pull towards the east. I let him off leash as we were going east. Deputy Hammar informed all units over the radio that he saw the suspect running towards 3900 E. away from the airport, the same direction that I was going. Bizi was in a fast trot, and I was close behind.

We came to a spot in the fence where Bizi stopped, puffed his chest, perked his ears up, and looked to the north. I looked to see where Bizi was looking, and there was a large pile of tree branches. As I looked over, I saw Joseph stand up from behind the tree branches with his hands in the air. Bizi started barking at Joseph, I informed him that he was under arrest and to start making his way towards me, and if he made any sudden movements, I would send the dog after him. Joseph stated he did not intend to run and made his way peacefully over to me. I laid Bizi down next to me as I instructed Joseph to climb over the fence, and then I had him put his hands on top of his head, go down on his knees, and then onto his stomach. I kept Bizi far away from Joseph, reinforced his down, and then approached Joseph handcuffed him, checked for tightness, and then double locked, so they didn't get any tighter. I rolled Joseph over to his butt and had him stay seated until other units could assist. Deputy Hammar, Deputy McRae, and Sgt Gonzales arrived. I attended to Bizi as they took Joseph into custody. And I returned Bizi to my vehicle, nothing further at this time.

K9 Cpl. A. Cleverley
Jefferson County Sheriff

I took Bizi away from the vehicle and placed him back in my patrol car. 

Deputy Teague searched the vehicle and did find anything that Bizi would have indicated on. I asked the subject when the last time something was in the vehicle and he wouldn’t give me a straight answer. I asked him when he used last and he had told his probation officer he had used earlier this day. I asked the driver of the vehicle the same question and he stated that he always had marijuana with him. I spoke with Deputy Teague and he told me again that the individual had used just prior to being stopped, nothing further at this time.

At approximately 5:37 PM on January 13, 2023, in the city of Roberts, in the county of Jefferson, I, along with other deputies, was dispatched to 2943 E. 650 N. for the complaint of a physical disturbance in progress. Having been to this address previously for a disturbance, I knew the male Christian Eduardo Gutierez (identified by his Idaho identification card) had a felony warrant out of Idaho Falls. I informed all deputies responding of the situation. Corporal Mathie and Deputy Salvesen were the first to arrive on the scene. Corporal Mathie told me that Christian had barricaded himself in the home's basement, and the female victim was in the shop.

Upon my arrival, I retrieved K9 Bizi from my vehicle and posted up on the southeast corner of the home as instructed by Cpl. Mathie. While we waited for more information from the victim. Sergeant Gonzales informed all on the scene that he would try to make contact at the front door. When Sergeant Gonzales knocked on the door, the door swung open, and I brought Bizi to the doorway and laid him down inside the doorway. Sergeant Gonzales stated that he was ready to go in the home if I wanted to. I issued three loud commands that we were with the sheriff's office, had a K9, and that he would be bit if he didn't come out peacefully.

After I issued my warnings, we heard no sound coming from inside the home and slowly started to make our way through the home, with Bizi searching in front of us. Corporal Mathie informed us that the suspect was going to be down the stairs, and at the very bottom of the stairs to the right, there was a bedroom that he was going to be in. I came to the top of the stairs, issued the commands once again, and then released Bizi into the basement to search Bizi searched the basement and indicated on the doorway that they had told us the suspect would be in.

Sergeant Gonzales and I made our way to the doorway, where I retrieved Bizi, and Sergeant Gonzalas tried to communicate through the closed door. When there was no communication, Sergeant Gonzales warned that we would kick the door down and release the K9, and he would be bit. Sgt. Gonzales tactfully kicked the door open, and I gave Bizi the command to apprehend. I saw Christian lying face down on the bed, covered in a blanket, and his feet hanging off the edge of the bed. Bizi moved to Christians' feet and hit them with his nose several times before jumping up on the bed and running over the top of him. When Christian did not move, Bizi came back to my side.

Sergeant Gonzales moved to apprehend Christian and check on his well-being. I kept my taser on the suspect in case of sudden movement. Sergeant Gonzales pulled the blanket from Christian and issued warnings to show his hands. One hand was down by his waist, and the other was underneath the pillow. Sgt. Gonzales moved in, took control of both hands, and placed him in cuffs. It was at this time Christian awoke and asked what was going on. He was taken into custody without further incident for the felony warrant out of Idaho Falls and pending charges.

Due to Christian's passive nature, Bizi did not see him as a threat during the apprehension and therefore did not bite. Christian was highly intoxicated and had passed out on the bed. Christian was searched for weapons and then taken to Corporal Mathie's vehicle to be transported

On January 22, 2023, in the county of Jefferson, I was working passive apprehensions with K9 Bizi. I had Deputy Reeves from Jefferson county jail in a bite suit for this drill.

Deputy Reeves was in a full bite suit and then placed up on a tall table with his head in the corner, his arm hanging, and his legs hanging off. I then covered Deputy Reeves with blankets and instructed him not to move, talk, or scream unless Bizi started biting him. I gave Deputy Reeves instructions on what to do If he was actually bit outside of the bite suit Deputy Reeves stated he understood.

I got Bizi from my vehicle and brought him to the hallway entrance connected to the room where Deputy Reeves was placed. I gave Bizi a very light command, trying not to amp him up with the sound of my voice, keeping everything as passive as possible. I then released Bizi and gave him the command to apprehend. Bizi moved through the building opposite where Deputy Reeves was placed but then quickly came back.

Bizi entered the room, searched all around it, and then went to the table where Deputy Reeves was lying. Bizi sniffed Deputy Reeves's hand, got up on his hind legs, sniffed Deputy Reeves's head, and then proceeded to bite Deputy Reeves on his head. Deputy Reeves, as instructed, yelled out a real bite, and I came in to get Bizi. When I entered the room seconds after Deputy Reeves had yelled, real bite, Bizi had already moved to the arm, and I quickly got him off.

Corporal Clements and Deputy Barnetche were with me when I took Bizi away, and Corporal Clements and Deputy Barnetche checked out Deputy Reeves. Initially, because he had bit Deputy Reeves's head, I had called for medical, but then it was discovered that it was not needed as it was just a scratch on Deputy Reeves's head.

Deputy Reeves stated that he was OK and did not need medical. I took photos of the scratch on Deputy Reeves's head and then assisted him in getting out of a suit. In the future, other precautions will be taken to ensure that this does not happen again if a drill like this is performed in training. Nothing for you this time.

At approximately 6:28 PM on January 21, 2023, in the county of Jefferson, I was patrolling and passed a 2008 gray Honda Civic bearing license plate 1J82693 going north on Yellowstone highway. The vehicle was missing a headlight. I negotiated a turn, got in behind it, and activated my overhead lights to contact a traffic stop to inform them of the headlight.

A female was operating the vehicle when I approached the driver's side. When she rolled down the window, an odor of cigarette smoke and a hint of marijuana left the vehicle. I informed the driver, Rebecca Ann Wilding (identified by her Idaho driver's license) the reason for the traffic stop. Rebecca was smoking a cigarette, as well as her male passenger. I tried to see if I could smell the odor of marijuana but could only smell the cigarette smoke from the two occupants blowing smoke inside the vehicle. The male occupant stared straight ahead, smoked cigarettes, and blew smoke inside the vehicle. Rebecca was shaking, would not make eye contact with me, and seemed very nervous. Rebecca provided me her registration, insurance, and driver's license, and I returned to my vehicle to run the information.

Upon running, Rebecca's driver's license information, it was discovered that Rebecca's license was suspended for DUI from October 2022 to April 2023. I returned to the vehicle and informed Rebecca that her license was suspended and asked her if she knew. Rebecca stated that she did not know that her license was suspended. Both Rebecca and her male passenger were still smoking cigarettes. When I was at the window the first time, I watched Rebecca light a cigarette, and when I returned after running her information, the cigarette was nearly gone. The time in between was very short. I explained to Rebecca that she was going to get a citation for driving without privileges and asked the male occupant if he was a licensed driver, and he stated that he was. I asked if I could get his driver's license to confirm that so that once Rebecca got her citation, they could switch seats, and he could drive. The male refused to give me his name and information and stated that I did not need it and that he would call somebody to come and get them. I asked him why he did not want to give me his information, and he said I didn't need it. I explained that if I had him operating a motor vehicle, I needed to confirm that he was a valid driver. He stated again stated they would call somebody.

I returned to my vehicle, started to write a citation for driving without privileges, and asked for a second unit so that I could conduct a K9 search. With the behaviors that Rebecca and her male passenger were displaying, along with the odor of marijuana that I smelled. I had reasonable articulable suspicion to believe that there was a controlled substance within the vehicle.

When a secondary unit arrived, I returned to the vehicle. I informed Rebecca that I was going to run my K9 around the vehicle because of the behaviors they were displaying. I asked Rebecca if there was any reason why the K9 would indicate on the vehicle and explained to her that he was trained to indicate on the order of narcotics. Rebecca stated there was no reason that a K9 should indicate on the vehicle. I had her roll up her window and let them stay in the vehicle, as it was a very cold night.

I brought K9 Bizi from my vehicle, walked him past the driver's door, and placed him in front of the vehicle on the passenger side. I gave Bizi the command to search and, on the first pass, gave him a free air sniff with no presentations. When we rounded the back of the vehicle and started coming up the passenger side, Bizi's head flipped backward, and there was a clear change in behavior. Bizi stopped at the passenger door for a moment. I released his leash and kept moving around the front of the vehicle. Bizi moved past the door and came to where I was, where I started doing a presentation of the vehicle. When we passed the rear of the vehicle and were coming up the passenger side, Bizi immediately hit the crack of the passenger door, stopped, sniffed, and scratched. I moved away from him Bizi moved with me for a moment and then turned around and went straight back to the passenger door crack and started scratching before sitting, indicating that he was in the odor of narcotics. I took Bizi from the vehicle and put him back in my squad car.

Officer Parkinson and Sergeant Gonzales asked Rebecca and her passenger to exit the vehicle and stand by a fence on the east side of the road away from the vehicle. When I got up to them, I explained to them that K9 Bizi had indicated on the vehicle, and we were going to search the vehicle.
