I went to the driver's side of the vehicle, opened the driver's door, and when I poked my head in, I could smell the odor of marijuana. Sergeant Gonzales opened the passenger side door and then told me to come around to his side. I went around his side, and he pointed out a plastic baggie with a green leafy substance behind the passenger seat on the floor. The location of the baggie was at the exact location of k9 Bizi's indication. I retrieved the plastic bag, observed what was within it, and with my training experience, recognized it as marijuana. I asked Rebecca and Zachary whose substance it was. Rebecca stated she didn't know it was in there, and Zachary said it wasn't his.

Sergeant Gonzales moved his vehicle closer to the area and allowed Rebecca and Zachary to sit inside to stay warm while I searched. During the search, I only found several lighters and no other controlled substance besides the marijuana inside the small baggie behind the passenger seat.

I went to speak with both individuals and had Zachary step out of the vehicle. I informed him that I knew that he was on probation and that he did not identify himself to me. I was going to be contacting his probation officer and then informed him that Rebecca would be taken into custody for possessing a controlled substance and driving without privileges. Zachary allowed me to search his person for any contraband, and I found none. Zachary had called for a ride, and they had arrived on the scene, and I allowed him to leave.

I had Rebecca step out of the vehicle, and I informed her that she would be arrested for possessing a controlled substance within her vehicle. Rebecca stated that it had been at least three months since she had smoked marijuana and didn't realize that it was in the vehicle. I searched Rebecca incident to arrest and found no other contraband. Sergeant Gonzales then transported Rebecca to the Jefferson county jail. Rebecca's husband, Benjamin Rawlins Wilding, arrived on the scene and was confirmed to be a valid driver and took Rebecca's vehicle.

Upon arrival at Jefferson County Sheriff's office, the substance that was seized from Rebecca's vehicle was tested and came back presumptive positive for marijuana. It weighed in at 1.2 ounces. Rebecca Ann Wilding is being charged with driving without privileges, Idaho code 18–8001, a misdemeanor. Rebecca is also being charged with possession of a controlled substance, Idaho code 37–2732(C)(3). Nothing further at this time.

K9 Cpl. A. Cleverley
Jefferson County Sheriff

At approximately 10:52 PM on February 17, 2023, in the county of Jefferson. Deputy Hammar initiated a traffic stop on a vehicle with Idaho plate 029UTE, a silver Honda Civic. During Deputy Hammars' traffic stop, he had an odor of marijuana coming from the vehicle. Deputy Hammar asked if I was close by and if I could respond.

I was just up the road, and it didn't take long to get with Deputy Hammar on his traffic stop. Upon arrival, Deputy Hammar had already asked the driver to step out of the vehicle and had him secure in his squad car. With the information given, I took K9 Bizi from my vehicle and walked him up to the silver Honda Civic.

I took Bizi up, passed Deputy Hammar's vehicle, and made it to the rear of the suspect vehicle. Before I could continue, Bizi yanked to the passenger side of the vehicle and then came back to the driver's side and quickly sat, indicating that he was in the odor of narcotics on the back driver-side rear door. I took Bizi back to the vehicle and informed Dispatch that he had indicated that we would be doing a probable cause search for narcotics.

During the search, inside a backpack on the passenger side floorboard was a large white bag with two containers holding a green leafy substance with my trading experience known as marijuana. Deputy hammer found a glass pipe with a green leafy substance in it with the odor of marijuana and several other items of paraphernalia.

Deputy Hammar confiscated those items and then informed the driver that he was going to be taking him to the Jefferson county jail to do a standard field sobriety test to make sure that he was safe to be operating the vehicle as he had already confessed to Deputy Hammar that he had used marijuana earlier in the day. I stayed with the vehicle while the suspect's parents came to retrieve it. The Suspect's parents retrieved the vehicle without further incident. Nothing further at this time.

At approximately 2:28 PM on April 27, 2023, in the city of Louisville in the county of Jefferson, Corporal Thompson contacted me by phone and asked if I could come and do a canine search at Jefferson high school located at 529 N. 3470 E. CPL. Thomson informed me that an individual at the school had been vomiting and confessed to smoking marijuana. CPL. Thomson said that he had three vehicles that he had reasonable suspicion of believing that there were narcotics within them.

Upon arrival, I took K9 Bizi from my vehicle and let him free air, sniff the parking lot off leash. While moving through the parking lot, Bizi went to a white vehicle, license plate 2F 46629. Bizi moved around the vehicle and then indicated on the passenger. CPL. Thomson and I searched the vehicle and located paraphernalia. He informed me that that was the vehicle that the individuals had been smoking in, and the owner had produced the controlled substance and willingly gave it to CPL. Thomson.

I took Bizi and had him free air sniff the rest of the parking lot, and he indicated on another vehicle that was sitting next to the white vehicle, license plate J43456. We found the owner of that vehicle asked what was in it, and he stated that there had not been anything in the vehicle; the wind was blowing hard from the northwest, and nothing was found during the search in this vehicle.

All the evidence was located CPL. Thomson took to file for charges. Nothing further at this time.

K9 Cpl. A. Cleverley
Jefferson County Sheriff

At approximately 11:50 PM on April 27, 2023, in the city of Rigby in the county of Jefferson officer, Durkin made a traffic stop on an older model white pickup at the 320 on-ramps on Highway 20. Shortly after, Officer Durkin made this traffic stop. He ran the individual Jason Thomas, identified by his Idaho driver's license, which came back with a felony warrant out of Jefferson County, a felony warrant out of Colorado, and a felony warrant out of Florida. I started responding to Officer Durkin's location when he asked if I would respond to a K9 search.

Officer Durkin stated that the individual was sweaty and nervous and was moving inside the vehicle. Upon arrival, I brought K9 Bizi up to the front passenger light and gave him the command to search when we rounded to the driver's side; I noted that there was a change in behavior on Bizi when he sniffed high by the driver's side door; we continued and when we rounded the rear of the vehicle and started back up the passenger side he yanked went to the passenger door, went on his stomach and went up underneath the passenger side of the vehicle. He came out, sniffed the door crack, and then sat next to the passenger door; I praised Bizi and took him away, and on the way back to my patrol vehicle, Bizi rounded Officer Durkin's vehicle and pulled me back to the suspect vehicle back to the passenger side door, and again sat. I praised Bizi once again and took him away from the vehicle.

Officer Durkin questioned Jason about what could be in the vehicle, and he stated that there was nothing in there and he didn't know when the last time something was in there, we did a probable cause search of the vehicle, and nothing was located.

After Durkin explained that he had followed behind the individual on the side of Highway 20 after initiating his overhead lights for a good half mile, I took Bizi from my vehicle. I walked back to the side of the road, searching for anything that looked odd. During that walk, nothing was found, but on the way back, I got to my patrol vehicle, and Bizi pulled me towards the suspect vehicle and again sat at the passenger side door.

Officer Durkin transported Jason to the Jefferson County Sheriff's office to be booked on his felony warrants. Nothing further at this time.

K9 Cpl. A. Cleverley

At approximately 4:32 PM on April 30, 2023, in the county of Jefferson, I was dispatched to 197 N. 3950 E. for the complaint of individuals trying to kick in a door. The reporting party Casey J Medley (identified by his Idaho driver's license), stated that he could see two Hispanic males, trying to kick in the door of the abandon home to the north of his home

Upon arrival, I took K9 Bizi from my vehicle, and started going to the door. From the west fence, a Hispanic male (Gabriel I Avila, identified by his name and date of birth) came out of the gateway when Sergeant Gonzales arrived on scene and came from the north across the small ditch and apprehended that individual. I was going to Sergeant Gonzales when I heard a sound to the south of the home and went to investigate. I looked over the fence and saw four males (Osman Rogel, Marco Abrica, Ulises Munguia Murillo, and Cruz Hernandez, jumping the far south west fence in the corner of the backyard of the abandoned house. I shouted sheriff's office to stop, and they did not comply.

K9 Bizi and I started running south on the roadway through the reporting parties' yard when I saw the individuals on the canal bank to the west. I cut through the yard and onto the canal bank, and again announced that I was sheriff K9 and to stop. They failed to comply and kept running south on the canal bank. I issued another warning "Sheriff's office K9, and they would be bit if they didn't stop."

When the individuals ran south, I released Bizi and commanded him to apprehend. I continued running south to try to keep up after Bizi had been released, and when he caught the group, he hit one of them on the left side causing him to hit the ground. When the individual hit the ground, Biz looked at the other three, and they continued running south. Bizi looked back at me, trying to decide which target to go after. I recalled Bizi, and he came to me. I again commanded the group that the canine would bite them if they did not stop.

The other three running individuals stopped, turned around, and raised their hands. I had Bizi in a down as I approached the individuals. I explained that sudden movements would be considered hostile, and my dog would bite them. All four individuals complied, sat down, and I waited the arrival of Deputy Hammar.

:  At approximately 11:16 PM on August 19, 2023 in the city of Rigby in the county of Jefferson. I traveling south on Farnsworth Way when Officer Parkinson I asked my location. I could see Officer Parkinson going north on Farnsworth towards me and he informed me that the vehicle behind him was failing to maintain lane.

As I passed Officer Parkinson, I noticed the vehicle come over the centerline towards me and then jerked back into the lane. I flipped around to continue following the vehicle when Officer Parkinson pulled into a turning lane to have the vehicle pass him so he could initiate a stop. When I saw Parkinson did this, the vehicle followed, stopped behind him, and then quickly swerved out into traffic around in Officer Parkinson’s patrol vehicle almost clipping the front passenger side fender. Once the individual had done this, he swerved into oncoming traffic, almost coming head on with a black Ford pick-up, causing it to swerve off the west side of the roadway.

Officer Parkinson initiated his overhead lights as did I and we started trying to stop the individual. The vehicle was in oncoming traffic and then in the center lane before swerving in front of other vehicle that was heading north on Farnsworth Way cutting it off and then driving off the roadway into the fence bordering Farnsworth Way and Highway 20.

I came up behind Officer Parkinson, who had come to a stop behind the vehicle. When I noticed the vehicle was get back over the curb that it had jumped to keep fleeing. I went around Officer Parkinson and the other vehicles that had been cut off and pulled in front of the suspect vehicle, so that he was unable to move. 

I exited my vehicle, and when I did, so, I heard an Officer Parkinson giving commands to the driver of the vehicle to step out, and to show us his hands. The individual did comply, stepping out with his hands in the air, laid down on his stomach. I moved in and placed him in handcuffs. I did a cursory search of the individual looking for weapons and found none. The individual had a wallet on him, and he was identified as Dominik Skyler Coy (Identified by his Minnesota driver’s license.)

While handcuffing and searching Dominik, I could smell the odor of alcohol coming from him, and he was slurring his words, and when I stood him up to walk back to Officer Parkinson‘s vehicle, he was unsteady and unable to walk very well.

After Dominik was placed in Officer Parkinson Vehicle, Sgt. Gonzales arrived on scene and had walked past a window and saw what he thought was drug paraphernalia. I retrieve K9 Bizi from my vehicle, brought him to the front passenger headlight and then gave him the command to search the vehicle, we made a pass around the vehicle when we made it to the backside of the vehicle Bizi jerked his head back, change his behavior and then move back to the driver side. He sniffed around by the driver side door and then continued back towards the back of the going up the passenger side of the vehicle, which was very close to the fence, bordering Farnsworth and Highway 20 because of the tightness in between the fence in a vehicle. I was unable to follow Bizi down that space. I turned him around, brought him back to the front of vehicle and had him go down the passenger side vehicle from the front Bizi went to the rear passenger door, sniffed high, then low and then sat on the passenger side door, indicating he was in the order of narcotics, and then started scratching at the door. I brought Bizi away from the vehicle and replaced him back in my spot in car.

During the probable cause search of the vehicle control test, senses, and paraphernalia were found as well as open containers inside the vehicle. Individual was transported to the hospital to be cleared medically to be brought back to the Jefferson county jail nothing further at this time.

K9 Cpl. A. Cleverley
Jefferson County Sheriff

At approximately 9:49 P.M. on September 22, 2023, in the county of Jefferson. I was patrolling with my trainee, Deputy Black, when Corporal Mathie tried to initiate a traffic stop. The vehicle that Corporal Mathie was trying to stop failed to yield and sped up at a higher rate speed. Corporal Mathie stated that the vehicle had been up to unsafe speech and was continuing down 800 N. in pursuit.

Deputy Black and I were on Highway 48, coming into Menan with Corporal Mathie, and he asked us to respond to areas 3300 E. and Highway 48 to try intercepting the vehicle. Deputy Salvesen was in front of us, and we started responding.

While around that area, Corporal Mathie stated the individual had gone through the stop sign on 3300 E. and Highway 48 and continued south down 3300 E., a dead-end road, and crashed the vehicle.

Upon arrival, Corporal Mathie had the individual out of the vehicle and at gunpoint. It was later discovered that the individual was walking away from the vehicle and sticking his hands in his pockets, requiring Corporal Mathie to move in on the situation and take control.

I retrieved K9 Bizi from my vehicle, approached the other units, laid him down, waited until he was secured in custody, and then returned Bizi to my vehicle.

Deputy Black, Deputy Salvesen, and I searched the vehicle while Menan QRU checked the suspect out, who was identified as Anibal Galaviz (by his Idaho driver's license). We could not locate anything inside the vehicle and called for a tow. Deputy Salvesen and Corporal Mathie checked en route to the Jefferson County jail. Corporal Mathie transported the suspect.

Hooked up, towing, arrived on the scene and retrieved the vehicle without incident—nothing further at this time.

K9 Cpl A. Cleverley
Jefferson County Sheriff

I did not want to stop until he got it right. Finally on the last send, I sent him then gave the down command within a couple seconds and did not let him get to far out this time. He downed. I hooked him up, and dismissed the agitator. I then praised him up like crazy and ended on that.

Worked on his down in motion again, this time by trying to use a blanket over the top of a hurdle at the school to break his train of thought some after sending him on the bite. I tried correcting him and he would start to go down but then run through it. At the end, I would send him and within a second of sending him give him the down command. He went down. It seems if he gets to far out, he just wants to go no matter what. Need to fix this.
RAN ROCKY AROUND THE VEHICLE AT THE REQUEST OF ISP. THERE WAS NO ALERT ON THE VEHICLE.

Went back out to the middle school and to work on his down in motion again. This time I hooked the long line up to him as well as having his e-collar. At first he was running through to the bite but I used the combo of the long line and e-collar to correct him, giving him a bigger correction then he is used to. I brought him back and tried again. Once again got the same correction as the first time. On the third attempt he went to a down when I told him to without any corrections. I moved up close to him and he took off. He was corrected on it. 4th time he went down and stayed down until I got him hooked back up. No correction was needed. I did it again, and he went down without correction. I was not holding the leash anymore either. I moved up, sent him on the bite again, let him run further out and then gave the down command. He went down without correction again. I dismissed the agitator, and then praised him a lot while bringing him back to the vehicle.

Went to work on his down in motion again today at the office. After last night I wanted to try again since he got a win last night. Used the same method as last night with the long line. First send he had to be corrected on. The times after that he went to a down when told. I then let him go get a bite as his reward.

Worked down in motion again at the school. Used the long line on him again. On the first send, he tried running through the down command so he was correctted on this. The second send he downed when told. Took the long line off him, and sent him again. He went to a down without any corrections at all. Rewarded him by letting him bite.

RECERTIFICATION DAY - PASSED! 

Started out doing the narcotics recert at Central Fire. First hide was in a box at the bottom of the book shelf in one of the offices. Rocky located this hide which was 48.8 g of marijuana without issues. We then moved to the next room over and there was no alert or change of behavior from him in that room so we moved to the womens bathroom. Rocky alerted on the cabinet in the bathroom which contained 5.5 g of cocaine. Then went to the mens bathroom. Rocky alerted on the toilet paper holder which held 10.75g of meth in it. I then called the second room as the blank room. From there we did the boxes. I burped each box first then ran Rocky down them. Rocky alerted on the 5th box in. I called this and was told this was correct. The box held 58.3g of heroin. I then started the vehicles. The first vehicle Rocky alerted up under the vehicle on the driver side door. I called this and was told it was correct. The hide was 38.9g of meth. The third vehicle, Rocky had a huge head jerk and came back to the compartment on the rear driver side area. He alerted on it. I called it and was told this was correct. The hide was 18.5g of heroin. The fourth vehicle was placed under the right foot area of the mobile command. Hide was 6.8g of cocaine. Rocky alerted on it when I was passing by the area doing a detail. I called the area and was told this was correct. Last hide was outside in the sprinkler box. I took Rocky off leash and sent him in the area. He ran right to the box and alerted on it. I called it was told this was correct. The hide was 72.7g of marijuana. 

We passed our narctoics certification.

RECERTIFICATION DAY -- PASSED!

We then started the recert for the patrol portion. This consisted of on and off leash heeling, down in motion, sit or down for 5 minutes, jump with stay, gunfire drill, building search, open area search, a call off without contact, a call of with contact and handler protection drills. Rocky passed each of this.

While en route I had dispatch ask if Tanner had seen the gun. Tanner said he didn’t know what it was but the guy pointed it at him before running around the back of the house. As we got closer dispatch advised us that there could be a suspect vehicle that was an orange charger 2023 registered to an Alexis Michele Rowberry (identified by her name and date of birth). Tanner stated that was his ex-girlfriend and he had seen it in front of his home the day prior and she was trespassed. Tanner said that Alexis had threatened to kill him and he suspected that the individual at his home was sent there by her. 

Upon arrival, Deputy Hall and I parked east of the residence and Cpl. Barnetche and Deputy Page parked about 50 yards behind our squad car. We exited our vehicle and I retrieved my rifle and we made our way to the home. We split in two pairs, Deputy Hall and myself and K9 Bizi designated team one and Cpl Barnetche and Deputy Page designated team two.

Team one moved around the south east corner moving north to the rear of the home we moved to a small open shed and continued further past the home to a garden area. We started moving back west behind the home when Tanner yelled out the back window to check the ditch on the far back part of the property. We told him to shut his window and secure it. We moved to the back part of the property when Team two stated they had found an open door on a shop further behind the home. 

We rendezvoused with team two and stack on the shop door. I moved to the door laid Bizi down and issued commands. When no one answered I sent Bizi into the shop to search for the suspect. Bizi searched through the shop and did not indicate on anything inside. Both teams moved to a camper where I issued commands and sent Bizi into the camper. Bizi once again did not indicate and we split again with team one north of all the homes checking back yards and team two check the front yards and buildings on the front side. 

Team one moved east from 4200 east through back yards checking out buildings and ditches. We moved all the way to 4221 east with no success of finding the suspect. Team two had some suspicious vehicles that passed by that they had City units check and see if the occupants match the description and they did not. Once we had cleared the area the best we could we returned to our vehicles and team two left to patrol the area for the suspect vehicle while team one went to speak with Tanner.

Hid an agitator in a small room behind some tires with the lights off. I sent bizi into the room for him to search. He moved slowly arounnd the room before he started coming back towards me. I re issued the command and he went further into the building. He eventually found the agitator and did a good fulll bite.
basic obedience.
basic obedience
basic obedience
basic obedience

source was hidden in a cabinet in a large room. I brought bizi to the opening and allowed him to free search the room. Bizi ran past the caninet and his head flipped back and he turned and started sniffing the cabinet up and down. He then started scratching and barking indicating that he was in the odor of narcotics.
with the new trainee we did building clearing and tactical obedience inside the fire station. Bizi broke and came to my side a few times but over all her did well.
basic obedience.

While working on my vehicle in the sally port. I had Rocky out of the vehicle in a down with everyone else walking around the area and next to him. It was a great training to make sure he stayed in the dowm with several others besides myself walking next to him and all around the area. He didn’t break the down until I told him he could. He actually stayed in a down for close to an hour.

Doing a bark drill with agitator hiding inside of the building. I gave commands for him to show himself and when he didn't I sent Rocky in to hunt for him. Rocky hunted the building and was able to locate the storage room the agitator was in. He then began to bark to alert me he had located the subject and wanted to get to him. We did a few "peak a boos" with the agitator to reward him with and ended the training.

Worked on his 3 phase out using the bite pillow. He did very well letting go off the bite during the commands and going to a down. I would then play with him with the pillow some and then give him the commands again. Did not have any issues coming off the bite.

Laid 2 short tracks through the yard out to the field. Each track had 2 turns in it. He did well with the first track staying on it including the turns. On the second track, he came off it at the second turn but was able to locate it again on his own. I watched as he got closer to the track there was a big head jerk and he went right to it.

Had cotton balls with odor on them and placed them outside under the container. After letting them sit for 30 min, I took Rocky outside and placed him down-wind of the container. I gave hi the command to search and he took off running around the container searching it. As he got closer to the hide, I noticed him starting to bracket the air with his nose more and started jumping up on the side of the container thinking the hide was up higher. He came back turned around and as he passed the hide area, had a head jerk back and started working the odor on the ground, getting under the container. He located the source and laid down on it staring at the area.

Worked more on his heeling. Same thing he normals does, wanted to run out in front of me some but he stayed close by. A couple times I had to correct him with the e-collar as he started to run out away from me. After the corrections he did well staying by my side.

I placed a hide under the table in the break room. I took Ricky into the break room and let him search the area on his own. He did well with locating the hide within a couple minutes and alerted with a sit.

Used the building as a blank area to do a person search. I made sure there wasn't anyone in the building before deploying Rocky. I took him to the door and gave commands for them to come out or identify where they were. I then sent Rocky in the building and let him search it. He hunted the entire building until he showed signs of being tired. I then called him back to me and took him outside and praised him up

Took Rocky out to search a truck that marijuana had been located in at a buisness. I ran Rocky on the inside of the vehicle and he was trying to get everywhere. I could tell he was in odor all over the inside of the vehicle by the way he was acting and sniffing around. He just could not pin-point one area until he hit the floorboard where the marijuana had been located. Found signs in the vehicle the driver of the truck had been smoking inside and the entire vehicle smelled of odor.

Placed some cotton balls with odor inside a tin can and then up under the bumper of the fire truck. I took Rocky inside and placed him in a down at the front of the vehicle. No wind blowing around so I just sat there for a few minutes and watched what he would do. I noticed he started to bracket the air and then really slowly started to get up and walk towards the vehicle. Once he did that I know he was in odor and gave him the command to search. He ran down the side of the truck to the back of it and hit the hide right away going to a sit alert. I rewarded him on this

Worked on his down in motion using the balls. I would throw one out and send him to get it. After a couple minutes of us playing fetch, I threw the ball and gave him the down command as he was going to it. He went to a down right away. I then allowed him to go get the ball. I did this several more times and each time he would go to a down.
Laid one longer track with 4 turns in it. He did very well staying on the track and working it. He did his normal zig-zag pattern but stayed with it the entire time.

Worked his down and stay and heeling. Again, wanted to run out in front of me during the heeling and when I tried to walk faster or go to a slow jog, he wanted to play and would jump up on me. I corrected him with the e-collar and after that he did well staying with me. No issues with the down and stay

Took him out to the church for a different location to try and work on his heeling. Same as normal. A few corrections with the e-collar and he started to stay with me much better. I also worked on his call back after putting him in a down, I would walk away and then call him to me. Making sure he didn't run right by me but came next to me.

Placed some cotton balls with odor behind a bag of cat food in the pantry. The cotton balls were inside a shoe behind the bag. I took Rocky into the area and gave him the command to search. I began by detailing the area with him. As we got near the source of the odor. He used his nose and moved the bag of cat food out of the way and went straight to the shoe. He buried his nose inside of the shoe, then came out and sat and stared at the shoe. I rewarded him.

Worked on him coming to my location after popping his door open from the patrol vehicle. We did not do this long due to the extreme cold and I noticed him trying to lift his paws up and keep them off the ground. His paws were getting too cold the longer we did it. But he had no issues running to my location once I popped his door open

Worked with the east idaho k9 teams and worked vehicles and patrol work. Rocky did very well locating the hides and doing what he needed to do with the patrol work. Had to correct him a few times. But he did great throughout the day.

Placed a hide of cotton balls w/ odor on them outside under the trash can going into the courts. I let Rocky out of the vehicle and gave him the command to search the area, letting him run around on his own. I noticed once he got down wind some of where the hide was at, he jerked his head back and started to work the air as he got closer. His head was braketing back and forth as he went. When he got closer to the trash can, he first stuck his nose near the top but then went down and smelled the bottom. He then knocked over the can, smelling the cotton balls then going to a sit.

Hides were 24.5 grams of Marijuana. Hide was outside in the gun lock box as you entered the building. As I was bringing Rocky into the building, as he began to walk by the lock box, I noticed a head jerk back to it. He jumped up and smelled the box using deep inhalations and then alerted in a sit and stare. 
2.31 grams of heroin hidden inside the pencil sharpner in one of the pods. I turned Rocky loose in the room to allow him to search on his own, I then began to detail the room. Once we got to the sharpner, he sniffed it hard and sat. I called the hide and it was correct. 
6.1 grams of meth hidden under a bed in the pod. I allowed Rocky to search the room on his own. As he was running past the bed, I noticed a head jerk back towards it and him begin to bracket the air as he walked towards the bed. He sniffed up under the bed and then went to a down alert. I called this as the hide, was told it was correct. I rewarded him. 
5 cotton balls of meth odor behind the pannel in the shower. I was detailing the room and entered the shower area, I presented up high and he sniffed the pannel and then began to scratch at it. I called this and was told it was correct. I rewarded him. 
2.55 grams of marijuana hidden in the dispatch area. Took Rocky inside and detailed the area. As I got to the hide, he began to use deep inhalations and then sat and stared at the source of the hide. I called this and was told it was correct. I rewarded him.

Worked a couple bark drills with the agitator hidding behind a door Sent Rocky in and allowed him to search the area on his own he located the agitator and began to bark once he found out he could not get to him. Allowed agitator to open the door and give him a bite.

Used the bite pillow to work on bark drills. Did not have any issues barking in order to get the pillow. Once he had it, I would then give the commands for a 3 phase out. He did well and would let go when needed.
Spent some time at Road and Bridge working on door pops. There were more places for me to hide at so I used them to hide from him and see how he did finding me. He did very well.

Laid a track through the yard and had 2 turns in it. Started Rocky on the track and he did very well staying with it all the way through. He did his normal zig zag pattern over it but never lost it, even stayed with it well on both turns.

Hide was inside of a wallet that was then placed in the back of the chair in the court house hallway. I gave Rocky the command to search the area and let him search it on his own for a few minutes before I began to detail the area. Once I detailed the chair, he showed a lot of interest in it but did not alert right away. He would run off then head jerk back to it, using deep inhalations on the chair again then move on again. The chair was the onlt place he was doing this. I burped the chair and then he got to the back of it and finally alerted. I called this as the area of the hide and was told it was correct. I rewarded him.

Spent the day working on building searches and bark drills some more. Worked various different drills from "run aways" to "high hides" and anything else we could think of besides just bark drills. Rocky had no issues going into the building and searching it on his own and then barking when he located the agitator and could not get to him. Other areas where he could get to the agitator he would engage and get the bite. Did choke/chase offs once he was off the bite.

Jail asked if I could run Rocky over severl bags of books that were brought into the jail to be donated. They wanted to make sure he did not alert at all on the books before taking them back. The books were placed in the hall way near visting and I took Rocky in the room and gave him the command to search. I ran him past the books several times as well as other areas in the room, he never alerted to anything. The books were clear.

Placed the hide outside up under the base of the light pole near the door to the fire station. After letting it sit for a little bit I gave Rocky the command to search the area while keeping him on leash. I took him through the side of the building and by the door, as we ran by the pole, I noticed his head jerk back towards the pole. He kept search the base of the pole for some time and then would begin to move away from it but then turn around and come back to it again. He then got up higher near the hide and began to use deeper inhalations near the base of the pole where the hide was at. He then went to a sit alert. I rewarded him.

Laid a track with 4 turns out throught the yard going towards the back of the field ending near the tree. I let it sit for 30 minutes then ran Rocky on it. He did well for the first little bit sticking with it but at the third turn he lost the track for a short period of time. He was able to pick it back up on his own and lost it again on the last turn. I let him work it out on his own again and he was once again able to pick it back up and stuck with it till the end.

Had cotton balls with odor on them and placed them in various places in the house. First hide was in the laundry room near the dryer sheets. I took Rocky in the room and gave him the command to search. I ran him around the room and as we ran past the area of the hide, he showed a head jerk back towards the hide. I kept moving him along then detailed the room. Once I presented the area of the hide, using deep inhalations, he stayed with the hide and then alerted on it. I rewarded him. Second hide was in the pantry area behind some food. I took Rocky near the area and gave him the command. Because of what was in the pantry I started with a detail of the area. The hide was on the top shelf. He did get in odor and alerted on the hide. Last hide was under the couch in the living room. This time I put him in a down and walked the room. I then gave him the command to search and let him search on his own. As he was running around the room I noticed the head jerk and run back towards the area of the hide. He kept trying to get under the couch and when he couldn't he laid down and stared at the source of the odor. I rewarded him,

Worked on down and stay and heeling with him. Had no issues with his down and stay. Longest time I let him stay down for was 20 minutes and stayed the entire time. During the heeling he did as usual and wanted to run out in front of me. Had to correct him a few times with the e-collar and after the corrections he did better at staying near my side.

Placed a hide under a a small pile of grass in the middle of the field. Hide was cotton balls with odor on them. I took Rocky outside and while on long line I gave him the command to search. He ran around the area on his own. He kept going back and forth running from one side to the other. He then ran past the hide while running to the other side of the field. As he ran by the hide, he showed a head jerk and began to bracket the ground working his way towards the area of the hide. Once he got to the hide, he alerted on it going to a down and stare. I rewarded him.

AT THE REQUEST OF BCSO, I ASSISTED WITH A SEARCH OF THE SCHOOL WITH OTHER AGENCIES IN THE AREA. ROCKY ALERTED ON 4 LOCKERS BUT NOTHING WAS FOUND INSIDE OF THEM. SRO CONFIRMED SHE COULD SMELL THE ODOR OF MARIJUANA COMING FROM THE ITEMS IN THE LOCKERS JUST NOTHING WAS FOUND INSIDE OF THEM

Spent the morning in the BCSO hanger working narcotics hides. I will attach what the hides were and the amounts at the end of this as soon as I am told what they were from the trainer that put them out. The first hide was inside of an automatic pop toy box next to 3 other boxes just like it. I ran Rocky down the boxes without presenting anything. As he ran past the box that had the hide in it, he showed a big head jerk back to it and then stuck his nose inside of the box for several seconds before pulling it out and going to a sit alert. The toy was then released from the box to reward him. The second hide was in a small tool box in the middle of two other tool boxes. It was a very small amount that was in the box. As I ran him past the boxes, he sniffed them on his own. When he sniffed the middle box where the hide was at, he started using deep inhalations on it but then moved on to the next tool box, before making it to the next box, he went back to the middle box, sniffed it again then sat on it. I called this as the source of odor and was told this was correct. I rewarded him on this. The third search area was down a few of the vehicles in the hanger and along the back wall at the end. I ran Rocky down the vehicle and boat taking him towards the wall at the end. On the wall was a small dirt bike. I presented the dirt bike and went to move to one other item but Rocky stayed on the dirt bike sniffing all around it. I tried getting him to come to me but he continued t work the dirt bike placing his nose up under the seat of it and then going to a sit alert. I called this as the source of the hide and was told this was correct. I rewarded him. Fourth search area was along a different section of the hanger along the wall moving down the wall. I began at the start point and started detailing the area with Rocky as there was a lot of items in the area to search. As I moved down the wall, I presented an ammo box sitting on the floor and then began to move to the next area presenting it for Rocky. Rocky stayed with the ammo box using deep inhalations on the box and then going to a sit alert on it. I called the box as the source of odor and was told this was correct. I rewarded him. Fifth area was in the small laundry area in the hanger. I took Rocky in the room and with it being smaller, I gave him the command to search and let him search on his own. After a few minutes of him not really alerting to anything, I began to detail the room by presenting everything to him. He started to show a lot of interest in the back of the water heater up high near the top of the pipe but did not stick with it, he then moved to trying to jump up higher near a door going into the bathroom. I detailed the room but still did not alert on anything. After making sure the hide was not high, I detailed everything again. I then presented down low on a pipe and got him to stick his nose inside of it. He finally alerted on it. I called that and was told it was correct. The air flow through the pipe was coming out near the top of the water heater where he was showing interest before and where he kept trying to get to before. Other dogs in the training where doing the same thing.

Took Rocky out to the high school again near the soft ball field and worked on door pops with coming out and finding me in various different locations. After finding me, I then would give him the command to return to the car on his own and get back in his kennel in the car. At first he did not want to return to the car on his own but with a small correction one time, he did as he was told and did so every time after that without issue. He would wait inside of the kennel for me to return and close the door waiting for the next door pop.

training.Location: Ammon Field Office / Lincoln High School
training.Notes: Had our K9 Conference meeting to start the training day off to discuss the upcoming conference and what needed to be done for it. From there we went to Lincoln High School and conducted a school search of the parking lot and some of the classrooms inside of the school. Rocky alerted on two cars in the parking lot. Not sure if anything was found in them or not. A known hide was placed under a car. The hide was meth. After the search I took Rocky to the car and had him search it. Once he alerted on it and tried getting up under the car to get to the hide. I rewarded him.

Worked on his heeling, down and stay, and recall. Had no issues with the down and stay and the recall, during the heeling portion, same as usual, wants to run out in front of me. Put him on leash to try and correct this before using the e-collar, but then he pulled on the leash. Used e-collar to correct him a few times each time he began to pull. After a few corrections he did better at staying by my side.

Laid a track with 2 turns in it. I also placed a couple small piles of cat food just outside of the track area to see what he would do as he came near the food. After letting it sit for a little bit I took him outside and ran him on the track. He did well sticking on the track, as we came to the first area that had the food near it, he did not pay attention to it and continued to work the track. The second area that had the food, he pulled towards the food but did not try eating it. It caused him to lose the track for a short time but was able to locate it again and continued on until he located his toy.

source hidden in the wheel well of county car at the sheriffs office. Not busy to the area laid him down. Then gave him the command to search did a pre-sniff around the vehicle first while maintaining a distance away from the vehicle. On the second path started doing a presentation. During that presentation on the rear passenger wheel this his head flipped. He started sniffing low and came back to the wheel. He sniffed around the wheel, and then sat indicating that he was in the order of narcotics.

Worked on his down in motion some after giving him a break. Started out by just throwing the ball and letting him go get it and bring it back. Then I would throw it, give him the down command and make sure he went to a complete down. He did this the first few times before I let him go get the ball. Towards the end, he did run through the command to the ball once and was corrected while he did it. I tried it again one more time and he did go to a down again without issues so I ended it on that

Had Cpl. Lundberg place several hides inside the sheriffs office court building and outside. The first hide was in the mens bathroom near the court rooms. I took Rocky in the bathroom and gave him the command to search it. Letting him search on his own. He first ran to the back stall and then came out and began to sniff around the bottom of the sink. As he got closer to the door he began to use deep inhalations and closed his mouth. He then went all the way under the sink and then came back out and sat staring at the back of the sink. I called this as the hide and was told this was correct. I rewarded him.

Hide was placed in the breezeway are between the courts and the annex building. I let Rocky search the room on his own as there wasn't much in there. He ran straight down the wall and as he began to pass the bulletin board, I noticed the head jerk and him coming back to it and he began to work his way up the wall bracketing the wall area. He then sniffed behind the board and sat. I called this and was told this was correct. I rewarded him.

Third hide was in the entry way area to the annex building inside the ice melt bucket. I let Rocky search the room on his own again. He was able to locate the hide almost right away without issue and pulled the cotton ball out then sat and stared at it. I rewarded him on it.

Hide was placed up under the back driver side of the vehicle. I took Rocky outside and placed him in a down near the vehicle downwind of it. I watched him and noticed he started to bracket the air with his nose. I then gave him the command to search and we ran around the vehicle. As we made our first pass around the vehicle, he showed a head jerk back towards the back bumper of it and pulled me towards it. I allowed him to go on his own at this time and using deep inhalations, he worked around the bumper of the vehicle and up under it near the wheel well. I at first froze in place and did not sit. I was waiting for him to sit but then noticed he wasn't sitting as he was standing in a puddle and did not want to sit in it. I rewarded him for his frozen stance and stare.
ASSISTED BCSO WITH SEARCHING THE HIGH SCHOOL. ROCKY ALERTED ON 2 VEHICLES IN THE PARKING LOT. UNSURE IF ANYTHING WAS LOCATED IN THE VEHICLES OR NOT

After making sure the fire station was empty. I took Rocky in and did a building search as if we were looking for a suspect in the area. I gave my commands then sent him in. I let him search the area on his own. He hunted the building the entire time, never returning to me until I called him back. I then prasied him up for his searching and we left.

While getting fuel at road and bridge, I placed a couple hides out on two of the vehicles. I let them sit for about 10 minutes then took Rocky near the vehicles to search. The wind was blowing really hard and as I got him downwind of them, he closed his mouth and started bracketing the air with deep inhalations telling me he was in odor. I gave him the command to search letting him go on his own. He ran straight to the source of the hide on both vehicles right away. Going to a sit alert on both. I rewarded him each time.

Door pop drills, making sure he would run to my location and then go to a down or sit. Once he did I would reward him with a toy then tell him to return to the car on his own. He did well and did return to the vehicle on his own each time.
basic obedience, as well as doorways
Doorways. Used treats to slow bizi down from blasting through doorways. This has been an issues with him lately.
BASIC OBEDIENCE
doorways and basic obedience. Bizi is doing better on doorways but it has to be heavily enforced.

sorce was hidden in a trashcan right inside the doorway. Utilizing the enforced down to not blast through doorways I laid bizi down and walked the room to see if bizi would move. I saw his head tilt back and he crawled forward sniffing. When I saw this I gave the command to search and he went deep into the room but quickly came back to the area of the trashcan searched around it then started scratching the trash can indicating he was in the odor of narcotics then sat further indicating he was in the odor of narcotics.
Blank sends into the build to heighten Bizi search drive. Once he searched for long period of time I took him put him up and rewarded him with a treat.
basic obedience
basic obedience
basic obedience
basic obedeince

Had my trainee hide in a room then I released bizi to search for him. It took a bit but eventually bizi came to the door and indicated that he had located the suspect by scratching the door then barking and sitting at the door.
had several people stand in the room to see how bizi did with passive apprehension. Bizi did not do well he ran all around the room without trying to apprehend.we will continue to work this drill.

Source was hidden in the library in a library book on the east wall. I brought busy to the doorway laid him down. I walked the room and then gave him the command to search. He moved throughout the room, coming back to me several times, and I had to give the command to search . I then started detailing the room. Once I started detailing the room, I came to the area where the source was busy started sniffing low along the bookcase before trying to scratch, and I had to pull him back. He then laid down, indicating that he was in the odor of narcotics. I had to pull him away, so that he didn’t damage the books.
basic obedience
basic obedience
basic obedience
basic obedience

source was hidden in a desk drawer in Dispatch. I released busy into the room told him to search and let him search the entire area. Busy kept moving around the area excitedly until I saw his head flip he came back to the corner of where the Storage jet was sniffed around, but then moved on. I came back to that area presented it Busy got on the legs sniff high and then low moved away, but then quickly came back. Started scratching them at indicating he was in the odor of narcotics.

Had a Deputy get into the bite soup and sit in the chair in the courthouse. I sent busy in to apprehend the individual, and he apprehended without hesitation. I did a three phase out busy complied with all commands, but when I moved into in the suspect busy reengaged, I got busy off the bite, laid him down and then had the agitator move away. I had the agitator come back in and attack me busy release is down and attack the agitator and then did another three phase out. We’re busy complied, and I had the agitator dismissed.
basic obedience
basic obedience

basic obedience

Source was hidden outside Ririe fire station magnet to a door. I let busy out of his cage to take a break, close to the doorway to see if while he was sniffing around to go to the bathroom he would catch the odor. After busy, he had finishes business he was running around, and as he ran past the door his head flipped back hard. He moved to the doorway with his nose, and sniffed around the doorway before scratching, and then sitting, indicating that he was in the odor of narcotics.

door, pop drills, Southfork Elementary. Stood on the backside of the elementary door popped busy and waited for him to find me. I could see him come to the corner, moved around a little ways and then ran back towards my vehicle. After about five minutes, he came back to the corner saw me and ran towards me on the backside of the elementary. All in all the drill lasted approximately 8 1/2 minutes.

several sources hidden. Source one was hidden in a bucket in the hallway. I brought busy to the search area, gave him the command to search, and he moved through it quickly. When I saw no changes of behavior, I started to present the areas on the wall , when I presented the bucket sniffed, it started scratching it and then laid down, indicating that he was in the odor of narcotics.

Second source was hidden under lunchbox with a sandwich and chips on the upper shelf of the lost and found. I brought busy to the search area released him to search. He passed by the lost and found once flipped his head back came back started scratching on the lost and found box before laying down, indicating that he was in the odor of narcotics.

Third source was hidden in a pair of gloves on a table. I brought busy to the third area had him move through the area on leash before releasing him to search on his own busy, kept searching underneath the table, and then would move away before moving back and searching under the table again. I tried getting him up on the table to indicate, but once he was on the table, he was too concerned about getting down. We moved the gloves to the floor. We’re busy, then sniffed them lay down indicating he was in the odor of narcotics.

Fourth source was it a hiding canister that appeared to be a sprite bottle. Release busy into the area off leash, commanding him to search for narcotics. Busy moved around the area before sniffing the can then sitting, indicating that he was in the odor of narcotics.

sources hidden at Southfork elementary. First source was hidden in the toilet paper dispenser in the second stall in the women’s bathroom. I released into the bathroom, commanding him to search for the order of narcotics busy throughout the bathroom before coming to the stall where the source was hidden, not knowing he could go through the door. He tried to jump over the stall and go under the stall. Once he figured out that the door was not locked, he pushed it open, moved into. At approximately 10:30 P.M. on April 12, 2024, in the county of Jefferson. Jefferson units were serving a warrant, and the individual (Carlin Andersen) had barricaded himself in the storage unit. They called for a K-9 unit to respond to assist in serving the warrant.

Upon my arrival at 11 PM on April 12, 2024. I spoke with the unit on the scene who informed me that there was a nighttime service active warrant for Carlin who had barricaded himself inside of the storage unit.  He was not responding to any commands. I was also informed that there was a second individual in there that was also resisting, any commands to come to the door. I was shown a copy of the warrant. I and the other Jefferson units came up with the tactical plan of assault to enter the building using K9 Bizi to apprehend Carlin as well as the individual resisting the command harboring, Carlin.

I took K-9 Bizi from my patrol car we got into a tactical column a four man team with me in the third space. We moved forward towards the middle door facing the west and stacked up 2 x 2 on either side of the door. Deputy Vernon opened the door I moved, K9 Bizi into the space of the doorway and issued my commands. I issued three commands all the same stating there’s a sheriff K9 in the door that would be released if they did not comply and come out. On the third command, A voice yelled out that they were coming to the doorway. I took K9 Bizi about 10 feet back from the doorway and let the other units call them out.

The units one by one called both individuals out, took them into custody, patted them down for weapons, and restrained them in handcuffs. I took K9 Bizi back to my patrol vehicle returning him without any further incident. Nothing further at this time.

K9 Cpl A. Cleverley
Jefferson County Sheriff

The individuals were Dustin Gene Lamb (identified by his name and date of birth) and Rhonda Renee Smith (identified by her name and date of birth). Both were on probation and during a home check methamphetamine had been found.
Upon arrival, I spoke with Officer Jimenez, he explained to me that they were doing a home check for Rhonda to make sure that she was still living at the address that she had provided, which was 698 N. 2700 E. During this home check Officer Jimenez opened a cooler and on top of sodas and ice, was a plastic baggie with a white crystallized substance inside of it. Officer Jimenez stated that Rhonda said it was a powder for pain for her teeth. After further questioning, Rhonda admitted that it was, methamphetamine and that she had used it earlier that morning.
Rhonda and Dustin were being detained inside the camper when I arrived. I informed Officer Jimenez that I had K9 Bizi with me and we could use him inside the trailer for further search. Officer Jimenez agreed and we had Dustin and Rhonda step outside the trailer. I detained Dustin in my vehicle and Rhonda was detained in Probation and Parole's vehicle.
I sent K9 Bizi into the camper. He sniffed around and immediately indicated where the cooler was sitting that had the substance in it. I praised him away from it and had him search further into the camper which he indicated on a closet door in the hallway and then as well as the bed in the upper portion of the camper.
I informed Officer Jimenez, what K9 Bizi had indicated on and then we went into the camper to search further. During the search, several butane torches were located as well as melted plastic pipes. During the search eight credit cards were found with names that did not match either Dustin or Rhonda. When asked about this later, Rhonda stated that the individuals had given her the cards to use. Two of the individuals are deceased, one being deceased for five years, but the card was still valid. Rhonda didn’t have any explanation to give at that time of why she had these cards aside from the owners gave them to her.
I read Rhonda her Miranda rights, which she stated she understood and was willing to speak with me. I asked her about the controlled substance and she stated it was methamphetamine. I asked her where she got it. She was unwilling to give information stating someone she knew. I asked her when she had last used and she stated that she had used it that morning in Roberts at the Mustang Center, Rhonda stated that she had used a glass pipe to smoke it. She then wrapped the glass pipe in a towel broke it with a hammer and then discarded it into a large trashcan there. Rhonda stated she did this so that no kids would find it. I searched the trash cans at the center and found no evidence of this. Rhonda stated that she had acquired the methamphetamine three days before this and on that day, she and Dustin used the methamphetamine in their camper located at 698 N. 2700 E. using the glass pipe which she states has now been destroyed. Rhonda stated that Dustin had nothing to do with acquiring the methamphetamine and that she acquired it solely on her own. Rhonda stated the pipe was hers and the butane torchers were hers as well.
I spoke with Dustin, and he admitted that he had used methamphetamine three days prior when Rhonda had acquired it. But he thought it was gone and didn’t know about any of the other paraphernalia. Probation and parole spoke with him further about his probation violations and I released him from my vehicle.
I took custody of Rhonda and informed her that she was under arrest for the possession of a controlled substance, which was a felony. Rhonda stated she understood I asked her about any weapons or anything that I might need to know about before taking her to the Jefferson County Jail and she stated she had nothing on her. I did a quick cursory checking for weapons, placed her vehicle and secured her with a seatbelt. Rhonda was then transported to the Jefferson County jail without further incident.
The controlled substance that Rhonda said was methamphetamine was weighed at 6 grams. Jefferson County is charging Rhonda Renee Smith with Idaho code 37–2732 possession of a controlled substance with the intent to use. Jefferson County is also seeking charges for. Idaho code 18–3125 criminal possession of a financial transaction card. Nothing further at this time.

K9 Cpl A. Cleverley 
Jefferson County Sheriff

At approximately 10:43 AM.0n 6/9/2024 I was contacted by Saint Anthony police officer officer, Hunter. Officer Hunter asked if K9 Bizi were they tracking canine. I informed him that he was and he asked if I’d be willing to come out to an area in Fremont county to use him on a track that was approximately eight hours old. I informed Officer Hunter that I was unsure if busy could find a track that old but if they wanted me to try, I would come and try. Officer Hunter stated that they did want me to come and try and informed me of the details of the case.

The information given to me was that Hispanic male was driving a Penske truck and I’d left it on the desert and fled out west of this area. Hispanic male had also left his eight-year-old daughter with the Penske truck. Officer Hunter stated that he had used his canine that had indicated on the Penske truck already and they were waiting for a search warrant to get into the truck. Informed me that the Hispanic male was very paranoid and started screaming that somebody was trying to kill him, and then took off Southwest into the desert, leaving his daughter there, this was a statement given to him by the eight year-old girl.

Fearing that something has happened to this individual Fremont county had activated their search and rescue and other surrounding agencies to assist. Upon my arrival, I got Bizi out of my patrol vehicle brought him to an area where the eight-year-old girl had stated they had laid down for a little while, laid him down and then gave him the command to search and track. Bizi slowly and methodically started moving back-and-forth around the area before taking off southwest, but still moving very slowly. I could tell that Bizi was on a track by the way that he had kept his head to the ground his nose to the ground and moving from one edge of a scent cone to the other by moving approximately 5 feet to one side and then back another 5 feet to the other side doing this in a pattern. When Bizi is in a pattern like this it’s an indication that he is onset of a track. We continued moving forward Southwest for approximately a half mile before we got to an area that we could no longer move forward. I put Bizi back up in my patrol vehicle. Turn the AC on and gave him water.

Idaho Falls Police Department arrived on scene with one of their canines to see if they could pick up the track from the point. We’re Bizi had stopped. They moved about 75 yards to the south before they started in a circle pattern not able to move any further because the ground disturbance and the heat were dissipating quickly and the track was now 10 hours old.

I spoke with a Fremont county lieutenant and told him of an acquaintance I had made with another individual a civilian canine handler who had a dog that could trail instead of track and asked if you’d like me to contact him. Lieutenant stated that he would like for me to do so , so I contacted Kevin Baugh.

When Kevin arrived, he took a sample from inside the cab of the Penske truck of the Hispanic males odor and presented it to his canine. His canine started off in the same track and same area that K9 Bizi and K9 Harry had already gone through. When we got to the area, we’re K9 Harry could not move any further , Kevin’s canine K9 Nikki continued south for at least a half mile before we came to a roadway and lost the track completely.

During Fremont counties investigation, they determined that someone may have picked up this Hispanic mail at the roadway. After this determination myself and K9 Bizi were no longer needed and we cleared the area. Nothing further at this time.

K9 Cpl A. Cleverley
Jefferson County Sheriff

When Deputy Bennett arrived, he found a young juvenile male who stated that his father was in the home's crawlspace at 4239 E. 100 N. Deputy Bennett asked the juvenile to go and get his father and waited on the outside of the crawlspace. When the juvenile came back? He stated that he couldn’t find his father underneath the home Deputy Bennett asked the juvenile what his dad’s name was. He replied Joshua Lee Bryson (identified by his name and date of birth). Deputy Bennett told the juvenile to go back under the home to see if he could find him and had Dispatch run Joshua. Dispatch came back with an active felony warrant for Joshua Lee Bryson.

The juvenile emerged and stated that he couldn’t find his dad under the crawlspace. With the information that Joshua had a felony warrant, Deputy Bennett issued a command for him to come out from underneath the home, or else Sheriff K9 was going to be sent in to apprehend him. Joshua then called out that he was coming out. Deputy Bennett took Joshua into custody and started walking towards his patrol vehicle. Joshua told Deputy Bennett that he was not allowed to go into his vehicle.

Upon my arrival, and incident to arrest I brought K9 Bizi from my vehicle and took him to Joshua‘s vehicle. On the first pass around the vehicle, we stayed 2 feet away doing a free-air sniff. We got to the rear of the vehicle on the driver's side when Bizi snapped back with a change of behavior, I then let him work freely down the driver's side, where he stuck his nose in the wheel of the driver-side rear wheel. At approximately 12:29 PM on October 10, 2024, in the county of Jefferson, I was informed of a wanted subject out of Bonneville who had two misdemeanor warrants and they had been confirmed. They informed me that the wanted suspect Thomas Chance Sanders (identified by his name and date of birth) was at his mother‘s home at 1491 N. 1425 E. in Terreton Idaho. I was also informed that a complaint had been called in the night before on October 9 at 6:18 PM. where Thomas could be seen on camera footage over three days coming in between the hours of 4 PM to 6 PM and stealing approximately three twisted iced teas from the cooler. This behavior went on for four days but three of the incidents were captured on camera.

I went to the location of the convenience store The Lube Shop located at 1341 E. 1500 N. in Terreton to speak with the manager, Tausha Bartlome. She showed me three separate videos where you can see Thomas come into the store in a large winter jacket. He goes to the far corner where the beer is located then he proceeds to put three to four twisted teas inside of his coat and pants. He closes his coat up, zips it up, and then takes one to the counter pays for one beer, and leaves with the rest concealed. After the employees became suspicious, the camera was moved above the beer cooler pointing down when Thomas came in on 10/9/2024 you could see him taking and putting the beer in his pants and his coat. I had Tasha email me the videos. Then I waited for the arrival of other deputies to assist in taking him into custody for the warrants.

When we arrived to take Thomas into custody at 1491 North 1425 East, he was inside of his mother‘s home. She allowed us to go into the home where he was taken into custody in his bedroom without incident for his warrants. He was read his Miranda rights and asked if he would talk with us about the incident at The Lube Shop and he declined. When we walked through the home, there was coffee and other things spread throughout the home. There had been shower curtains, broken, and other items inside the home broken. It appeared that Thomas had taken a roll of toilet paper, unraveled it in the bathroom, and urinated on it outside of the toilet.

Jefferson County Sheriff's office is charging Thomas Chance Sanders with Idaho code 18-1401A commercial burglary and Idaho code 18–7001 malicious injury to property for damaging his mother‘s home the night before. Nothing further at this time.

K9 Cpl A. Cleverley

At approximately 6:09 PM on October 10, 2024, in the county of Jefferson. I was dispatched to the 128-mile marker on I-15 to assist Idaho state police with a traffic stop with K9 Bizi. 

Upon arrival, ISP stopped the vehicle at the 128 southbound off-ramp right as I arrived. I took Bizi from my vehicle and brought him up to the vehicle that they had stopped to do a free-air sniff. 

I walked past the driver's side where I saw a head snap, but Bizi kept moving with me to the front of the vehicle. I went to the passenger side headlight and stopped there because Trooper Higley was speaking with the driver at the passenger side door. I turned around and moved back around the front of the vehicle down the driver's side, when I noticed the change of behavior I moved towards the vehicle, we passed the rear of the vehicle, where there was a head snap, and then down the passenger side where Bizi moved in towards the car, but I maneuvered around Trooper, Higley, and then back around the front of the vehicle. As we moved down the driver's side of the vehicle, something caught Bizi’s attention. He moved quickly down the driver's side, turned his head in towards the rear driver's side door, but continued. I saw the change of behavior. I brought him to flip him around to go back up and he went to the Rear of the vehicle right behind the rear driver's door and sniffed it had a large change in his behavior then got on the vehicle, scratching at it, indicating that he was in the odor of narcotics. When did this he had already had a change of behavior that I noticed which is why I redirected him with a spin and he went there on his own. Bizi started scratching at the vehicle his normal indication of narcotics, and to not damage the vehicle I pulled him away. He moved around the rear of the vehicle but quickly went back to the vehicle and displayed the same behavior in that area. Once he had done this. I brought him away from the vehicle, and let him take a break on the side of the roadway. I indicated to Trooper Higley that Bizi had indicated on the vehicle and then went to take him back to my vehicle when he pulled me back to the area and sniffed around I then took him back to my vehicle. 

Trooper Higley had the driver Joseph Angel Perez (identified by his Idaho driver's license) exit the vehicle brought him to the rear of the vehicle and asked him why a K9 would have indicated on his vehicle. Joseph stated that he had two THC vape pens in the vehicle one was in his pocket and he handed it to Trooper Higley. Joseph stated the other one was in a holder on the dash of the vehicle. Joseph admitted to Trooper Higley that he had recently smoked the vape with the THC in it so Trooper Higley put him through a standard field sobriety test to make sure that he was okay to drive.

Once the test was complete Trooper Higley went to get something from his vehicle while I spoke with Joseph. Joseph asked if he was in trouble and I told him that it was illegal to have marijuana in the state of Idaho. He told me that we could search the vehicle. Trooper Higley put Joseph in the rear of his vehicle and informed him that we were going to be searching the vehicle Joseph again stated that it was okay for us to search the vehicle. Upon the search, there was a backpack behind the driver seat at the rear driver-side door where K9 Bizi had shown interest and indicated. Upon a search of this backpack, there was narcotics and paraphernalia found within it. A white substance as well as a white powdery substance was located as well as two brown bottles with a clear liquid in them. 

Trooper Higley took Joseph out and read him his Miranda rights. Trooper Higley asked Joseph what the substances were and he told him meth and GHB. ISP detectives came and took him to their office for questioning nothing further at this time.

K9 Cpl A. Cleverley
Jefferson County Sheriff

At approximately 7:51 PM on November 18, 2024 in the county of Jefferson city officer Harris was dispatched to 198 N. Yellowstone, the location of Intermountain auto where the reporting party LaGrand Boone the owner stated that a recently terminated employee had arrived on scene Slipped under a fence and was now back in their salvage yard.

When Officer Harris arrived on scene, he located the vehicle belonging to the suspect, Cory Bluemel identified by his Idaho drivers license. LeGrand stated that that was his vehicle and that other workers had seen Cory slip under an opening in a fence. When I arrived, I updated the other deputies that were in route to the location, but it was confirmed that Kory was on the premises in the salvage yard. I informed DISPATCH that we were going to wait the arrival of the rest of the team before making entry into the building on the premises or into the salvage yard.

When Sergeant Gonzales corporal Barnetche and Corporal McRae arrived on the scene we quickly put together a plan, made entry into the building and went into the salvage yard. I deployed K9 busy from my vehicle and followed behind the team closely. myself and corporal Barnetche cleared a small shop while Sergeant Gonzales and Officer Harris cleared one further up from us. As we moved south through the salvage yard with the main building to the west of us there was a large banging sound inside of one of the shops.

Officer Harris and Sergeant Gonzales made their way to the source of the sound and announced themselves, the sheriffs office and the police department, and also announced that there was a canine make themselves known and follow the command or there was a possibility they may be bit. Corporal Barnett and I made our way over to Sergeant Gonzales and Officer Harris where we split again myself and Gonzales went further south around the side of the building to find an entryway into the shop to see if we could locate Cory in the shop where the noise was coming from.

On the south side of the shop, there was a door where me and Sergeant Gonzales made entry into a long dark corridor with doorways leading into each shop bay through the corridor. We checked each doorway as we move down the corridor before coming to an open door where I got into position, announce that there was a canine , and make themselves known and then release canine busy into the room. Deputy Donahue with Clark county sheriff’s office asked if I’d be able to come to a free air sniff with K9 Bizi. After speaking with Sergeant Gonzales, it was approved for me to go and assist Clark County. 



Upon arrival, I was informed of the full situation. At the gas station in Dubois, Idaho in Clark County off the exit gas station name Ikes there was a truck and trailer on the north side of the property and the owner of that truck and trailer Tyler Myers had been asked to leave and had not done so. A Clark County Deputy the day before December 8, 2024 had gone and asked Tyler to leave the premises. The Deputy observed a strange behavior from Tyler and gathered more information and discovered that he had recently been trespassed from an area in Idaho Falls for the same behavior where he was found with several individuals in possession of methamphetamines and fentanyl.



The Clark County deputy stated they were going to go back over make contact with Tyler and tell him that he was going to be trespassed from Ike‘s and while doing so asked if I would do a free air sniff when they make contact. Clark County made contact with Tyler and informed him that he was going to be trespassed and asked for consent for me to run my dog around his truck and trailer. Tyler consented to canine busy running around the vehicle and stated that it was OK if he touched it. When I brought K9 Bizi up to the truck and trailer, Tyler informed the Clark County deputies that there was paraphernalia in the trailer.



I started busy at the front passenger headlight. I laid him down and gave him the command to search, and we made our way around the vehicle as we were coming up the trailer side of the vehicle. I saw Bizi’s head snapped back towards the back of it when he pulled to the rear, tires, sniffed around, tried going underneath, and then came with me as I continued moving we made it to the rear of the truck and then to the passenger side door, where busy sniffed the crack of the door Underneath the truck, and then started scratching on the truck, indicating that he was in the odor of narcotics. I praised busy away from the truck took him back to where he showed interest on the trailer gave him the command to search when we got to the camper door Bizi sniffed underneath the camper door, then laid down indicating that he was in the odor of narcotics. I rewarded Bizi and returned him to my vehicle.



During the search a substantial amount of paraphernalia was located meth pipes, marijuana pipes prescription drugs, as well as a controlled substance of fentanyl controlled substance of an Adderall without prescription controlled substance of marijuana and other items used for drug use. During the search Clark County deputies took Tyler into custody for the possession of controlled substance and paraphernalia , impounded the vehicle for a more in-depth search of the trailer as they were finding something with every box that they opened. Clark County deputies stated that they no longer needed me on scene and I cleared nothing further at this time.

At approximately 5:59 P.M. on 2/6/2025 in the county of Jefferson. I was patrolling the area of 3747 east 369 north for a previous complaint of reckless driving when I saw a silver ford mustang at approximately 3730 east 369 north spinning around in the field west of me. 

I approached the vehicle and discovered that it was stuck and couldn’t move. I met with the driver Richard Faye Brotzman (identified by his Idaho Identification card). Richard stated he was out there looking for old scrap wood for burning in his woodstove. He stated that he didn’t realize that the ice he was on was a deep puddle and his vehicle broke through the ice and he couldn’t move. I assisted Richard to get his vehicle out of the puddle and back on the roadway. Once Richard was back on the roadway I gathered his information and I noticed that he had cigarettes and a vape in the vehicle. Richard was acting odd and then informed Sgt. Gonzales and I that he was on probation for theft and then further informed us that he was a recovering addict. I asked Richard if I could run K9 Bizi on his vehicle and he said I could and I asked if K9 Bizi could touch his vehicle and he said that he could. 

I brought K9 Bizi to the front passenger headlight of the vehicle and laid Bizi down. I gave him the command to search and we started to move around the vehicle. We moved down the driver side of the vehicle and around the back we moved up the passenger side of the vehicle and Bizi searched high and low. As we moved around the front of the vehicle for a second pass Bizi yanked back slowed down started sniffing the front of the vehicle then moved to the driver door where he sniffed high and low then sat indicating that he was in the odor of narcotics.  I took Bizi back to my patrol vehicle then did a probable cause search of the vehicle. 

I searched the vehicle and only located the vape and cigarettes. Richard was only 19 years old and stated that he has been able to purchase the vape and cigarettes without any issues and I informed him he must be 21 to purchase tobacco products in Idaho and he was given a citation for minor in possession of tobacco products. Nothing further at this time.
